item.description: arXiv:2611.02072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Conway--Guttmann formula for the generating function of $k$-convex polyominoes by semi-perimeter, for every $k\ge2$. A decomposition according to the two diagonal directions reduces the enumeration to convex polyominoes satisfying a one-bend condition in one diagonal direction. Splitting these polyominoes at the right endpoint of the top row leaves an initial part followed by columns whose vertical intervals decrease by inclusion. Ordered forests describe the initial part and retain the row information needed to determine when column extensions first exceed the prescribed bound. A first-passage calculation, together with a sum over initial parts already above the bound, gives the required generating function. The argument includes the case $k=2$.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Prellberg

item.title: Characterizing $k$-Naples parking functions and refining bounds via obstructed parking functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Naples parking functions are a major generalization of the classical parking functions, where cars have more options to park because they are allowed to check (and possibly park) backward up to a fixed number of spots before driving forward as in the classical case. In a previous work, using involutions we established an injection from the Naples parking functions to a special set of obstructed parking functions, which we referred to as \textit{left obstructed}, thereby immediately obtaining a crude upper bound on the former set. We continue that work here by identifying the image of this injection, providing a characterization of Naples parking functions as a certain (smaller) set of obstructed parking functions, which we will refer to as \textit{long left obstructed}. We also derive a formula for the number of left obstructed parking functions. These combined allow us to improve the upper bound on the Naples parking functions. In addition, we demonstrate how lower bounds for this set can be obtained. As will become clear, the long left obstructed parking functions have certain combinatorial features that are useful in estimating the cardinality of the set, which are not obvious from solely looking at Naples parking functions.
item.dc:creator: Roger Tian

item.title: A hitting-time version of Kotzig's conjecture in random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A family of perfect matchings on the same vertex set is said to have the Kotzig property if the union of any pair of matchings forms a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig famously conjectured that, when $n$ is even, the complete graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into $n-1$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. A closely related conjecture of Wormald states that, for fixed $d \ge 3$, whp a random $d$-regular graph contains $d$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. Recently, the first and third authors considered a version of these problems for the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ and proved that, for every fixed $k$, there is $C=C(k)$ such that whp $G(n,C\log n/n)$ contains $k$ perfect matchings with the Kotzig property. We strengthen this result by showing a hitting time version: for every fixed $k$, whp the hitting time in the random graph process for finding $k$ edge-disjoint perfect matchings with the Kotzig property is the same as the hitting time for a graph with minimum degree $k$. This is a generalisation of the celebrated result of Bollob\'as and Frieze for even $n$ establishing the hitting time for $k$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. The proof uses several ideas. We first design a coupling, via a randomised algorithm, of the random graph at the hitting time with $k$ almost-independent perfect matchings and a set of random reservoir edges, which may be of independent interest. We then prove various statistical properties of these matchings, in particular concerning the cycle structure of the $2$-factors formed by pairs of matchings. This includes a novel concept of ``shuffledness'', which we establish through a careful exposure argument and a concentration inequality for random permutations. Finally, we show that the initial $2$-factors can be merged into Hamilton cycles, using the random reservoir edges, by analysing certain P\'osa-type rotations via branching processes.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Glock, Lyuben Lichev, Amedeo Sgueglia

item.title: Graphs versus loopless digraphs with a given degree sequence, and convergence of uniformly random graphs at every density
item.description: arXiv:2611.02191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a degree sequence d on n vertices with M edges, let G(d) be the number of simple graphs and D(d) the number of loopless digraphs with in-degree = out-degree = d. We conjecture that G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d, a single inequality across all densities, and prove it up to an extra factor log n: G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n log(2+M/n)) for every graphical d. The proof compares pairs of graphs with Eulerian digraphs by alternately colouring closed trails; the failure of injectivity is measured exactly, shared edges cancel against 2-cycles, and parity is handled by merging trails and by a parity argument on Eulerian circuits of odd components. No asymptotic enumeration and no bound on the maximum-entropy multipliers is used. When the maximum-entropy edge probabilities lie in [delta, 1-delta], the same method gives the conjecture itself, G(d) >= sqrt(D(d)) exp(-C n log n / delta). Combined with the exact identity G(d) = exp(g*(d)) pi(d), where pi(d) is the probability that the maximum-entropy beta-model has degrees exactly d, and a van der Waerden-type bound for D(d), this shows that uniformly random graphs with degree sequence d are close in the normalized cut metric to their beta-model whenever M >> n log n log(M/n), at every density, with no tameness and no cap on the degrees. We also record the conjecture in the sparse regime and, with constant 1/2+o(1), in the dense tame regime, from the asymptotic enumerations of McKay-Wormald and Barvinok-Hartigan.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Mehrdad

item.title: The real eigenvalues of the non-backtracking Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.02194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $N$ nodes and $M$ edges, with minimum degree at least $2$. We prove that the non-backtracking Laplacian of $G$ has at least $2M-2N+2c+2b$ real eigenvalues, counted with algebraic multiplicity, where $c$ is the number of connected components of $G$ and $b$ is the number of bipartite ones. More precisely, at least $M-N+2c$ of them lie in $[0,1)$ and at least $M-N+2b$ lie in $(1,2]$. We show that the bound $2M-2N+2c+2b$ is sharp, and that a connected $d$-regular graph attains it if and only if it is strictly Ramanujan, i.e., every adjacency eigenvalue $\mu\ne\pm d$ satisfies $|\mu|<2\sqrt{d-1}$. For completeness, we also show that the non-backtracking Laplacian has at most $2M-2c-2b$ real eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Raffaella Mulas, Leo Torres

item.title: A Quasisymmetric Analogue of the Bruhat Order
item.description: arXiv:2611.02210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a quasisymmetric analogue of the Bruhat order on indexed binary forests using the multiplicity-free Monk rule for forest polynomials. For the finite window $\mathcal{P}_n$ of forests supported in $[1,n]$, we construct an explicit partition into saturated chains terminating at the top rank, proving that $\mathcal{P}_n$ is strongly Sperner. We also recover the known Catalan ballot formula for its rank numbers. For principal lower intervals, we prove that $[\varnothing,F]$ is a lattice if and only if it is Boolean, and characterize this property by the avoidance of a bent corner in $F$, a path of three internal vertices that changes direction. This gives a forest analogue of the pattern-avoidance characterization of Boolean principal Bruhat intervals. We also conjecture that every principal lower interval is shellable, providing computational evidence and proving the conjecture for a family of hook intervals.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Bansal

item.title: How the eigenvalue region of standardized Laplacians leaves the 2005 polygon
item.description: arXiv:2611.02249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of $n\times n$ standardized Laplacian matrices, and let $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ be the polygon introduced in 2005, with upper vertices $\lambda_0=0,\dots,\lambda_{n-1}=1$. It is now known that $\Lambda_n=S_n$, and that $\Lambda_n$ is convex, if and only if $n\le4$. We study how $\Lambda_n$ leaves $S_n$ near an edge $[\lambda_m,\lambda_{m+1}]$, $2(m+1)<n$. First, we prove a switching law for matrices having a boundary point of $\Lambda_n$ as a simple eigenvalue: an explicit switching function on the arcs, built from the left and right eigenvectors and the outward normal, forces maximal weight where positive and zero weight where negative; intermediate weights occur only where it vanishes. Second, we perturb the weights of the arcs $k\to k+m+1$ in the circulant digraph (arcs $k\to k+s$, $1\le s\le m$, plus these arcs with weight $\tau$) that realizes the point $\lambda_m+\tau(\lambda_{m+1}-\lambda_m)$. At second order, the first Fourier harmonic of the perturbation moves the eigenvalue beyond the line of the edge if and only if $\tau<\tau^*_m=\sin(\pi m/n)/(2\cos(\pi/n)\sin(\pi(m+1)/n))$. For even $n$ and $m$, the point with $\tau=\tau^*_m$ is the vertex of $S_{n/2}$ lying on this edge, and digraphs with these arcs only at even $k$ give an explicit eigenvalue path that leaves $S_n$ at $\lambda_m$ and, in all computed cases, ends at this vertex. Third, we give a conjectural, numerically supported picture of $\partial\Lambda_5$: beyond each edge of $S_5$ not incident to $0$ or $1$, $\Lambda_5$ forms a cap bounded by four algebraic arcs, which leaves the edge tangentially at its endpoint adjacent to $0$ or $1$ and rejoins it at $\tau^*_1=(3-\sqrt5)/2$; the rest of the edge lies on $\partial\Lambda_5$. In computations for $n\le8$, a cap returns to its edge smoothly at $\tau^*_m$, at a corner at $\tau^*_m$, or at a corner beyond $\tau^*_m$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Chebotarev

item.title: On Lattice Tilings by Symmetric Limited Magnitude Error Balls: Q-polynomials and Ideal Characterization
item.description: arXiv:2611.02394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the lattice tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by the symmetric limited magnitude error balls $\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)$, which play a crucial role in flash memory applications. Using generating functions and complete Bell polynomials, we derive an explicit formula for the $r$-th Q-polynomial associated with $\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)$. Then, an ideal-theoretic characterization of the lattice tiling condition is developed: for an odd prime $p$ dividing $|\mathcal{B}(n,t,k,k)|$ exactly once, a lattice tiling would force a certain polynomial to lie outside a certain ideal of $\mathbb{F}_p[Y_1,\dots,Y_{\frac{p-1}{2}}]$. Applying this criterion yields congruence conditions on the dimension $n$ that rule out lattice tilings; for $2\le t\le10$ and $1\le k\le10$, a systematic Maple computation over all primes $3\le p\le29$ excludes, on average, $35.65\%$ of all dimensions, with a maximum of $76.69\%$. Finally, we obtain two infinite families of parameters $(n,t,k)$ for which no lattice tiling exists: no lattice tiling exists if $k\equiv4\pmod9$ and the base-$3$ addition of $t$ and $n-1-t$ produces exactly one carry; and no lattice tiling of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by $\mathcal{B}(n,n-1,k,k)$ exists if $k\equiv8\pmod9$ and $n\equiv2,4\pmod6$. Their sizes are also estimated.
item.dc:creator: Ang Xiao

item.title: Minimum net-saturated graphs of even order
item.description: arXiv:2611.02399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(F\) be the net, consisting of a triangle with one distinct degree-one vertex attached to each of its vertices. A graph is \(F\)-saturated if it contains no copy of \(F\), but adding any missing edge creates one. Zhao, You and Zhang determined the minimum number of edges and conjectured that the minimum graph is unique at every sufficiently large even order. We prove that for every even \(n\ge12\), there are exactly four minimum \(n\)-vertex \(F\)-saturated graphs up to isomorphism, each with \(3n/2\) edges. Three additional families therefore disprove their even-order uniqueness conjecture. Two have no universal vertex, that is, no vertex adjacent to every other vertex. We also construct a ten-vertex minimum graph with fifteen edges outside the four families, proving that the threshold twelve is optimal. The key structural step forces a pendant triangle, meaning a triangle with two vertices of degree two, in every even-order minimum graph above order ten. We classify the graphs containing such a triangle and bound the order of all remaining extremal configurations by ten.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Cao, Chunxiang Wang

item.title: Dynamics of Transversal Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.02586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a way of generating matroids by randomly picking indicator vectors, and since we will see that it mostly gives uniform matroids, which are transversal, we then look at randomly generated transversal matroids. In both models we also investigate threshold phenomena of certain monotone increasing properties. Non-monotone properties of transversal matroids will also be investigated. Moreover, we are going to see how to spot circuits of a transversal matroid from its bipartite graph presentation. In the last Chapter, we have a survey of the characterization of transversal matroids that admit acyclic bipartite presentations. We will also investigate when we can simplify a presentation for a transversal matroid.
item.dc:creator: Hin Lon Lao

item.title: Spectral radius and size conditions for 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs to contain a $k$-factor with $k\ge 3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix $A(G)$ of a graph $G$ is called the spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of $G$. If $S$ is a vertex cut of a connected graph $G$, then $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of connected components of $G-S$. The toughness $t(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as $t(G) = \min\left\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}: S \subset V(G), \text{ and } c(G-S) > 1\right\}$. A graph \( G \) is \( t \)-tough if \( |S| \ge t c(G - S) \) for every proper subset \( S \subset V(G) \) satisfying \( c(G - S) > 1 \). Combining the toughness and spectral conditions, we provide spectral radius and size conditions for the existence of $k$-factors in 1-tough balanced bipartite graphs. This settles a problem posed by Chen, Fan and Lin in [Discrete Appl. Math. {\bf 355} (2024), 223--231].
item.dc:creator: Jinxuan Ren, Jiayao Song, Ligong Wang

item.title: k-uniform l-Eulerian hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider $l$-Euler trails and $l$-Euler circuits in finite $k$-uniform directed multihypergraphs, where $k\geq 2$ and $1\leq l<k$. Let $D$ be such a directed multihypergraph. The notions of $l$-connectivity and $l$-balance are defined in terms of the $l$-tails and $l$-heads of its hyperarcs. It is shown that $D$ is $l$-Eulerian if and only if $D$ is $l$-connected and $l$-balanced. Moreover, $D$ is $l$-semi-Eulerian if and only if $D$ is $l$-connected and has exactly two states with unequal $l$-indegrees and $l$-outdegrees, one with $l$-outdegree one greater than its $l$-indegree and the other with $l$-indegree one greater than its $l$-outdegree. The proofs are based on an $l$-transition digraph and the classical Euler theorem for directed multigraphs. The corresponding conditions for $k$-uniform multihypergraphs are also obtained in terms of their orientations. For a given orientation, an expected linear-time algorithm is provided to determine whether an $l$-Euler trail or an $l$-Euler circuit exists and to construct one when it does.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Lei, Chenxi Lv, Bing Dai

item.title: Every tournament $T$ of order at least 3 admits infinitely many $T$-irregular oriented graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a fixed graph. A graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if any two distinct vertices of $G$ belong to a different number of subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to $F$. In this paper, we settle the strong conjecture about $F$-irregular oriented graphs (Dovzhenok, Lukashenko, and Filiuta, 2026) for the case of tournaments. Specifically, we prove that for every tournament $T$ of order $n \ge 3$, there exists an infinite family of $T$-irregular oriented graphs. Our proof is constructive. For $n \ge 4$, it is based on the vertex cloning method, and the underlying graphs of the constructed $T$-irregular oriented graphs are inherently $K_n$-irregular.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Dovzhenok

item.title: Colorings breaking prescribed families of graph automorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every continuous action of a compact group on a discrete set, each finite-color template admits a coloring from arbitrary lists of the same size whose stabilizer is contained in a conjugate of the template stabilizer. Consequently, the ordinary and list parameters coincide whenever the ordinary parameter is finite. In particular, we answer the question of Ferrara, Flesch and Gethner negatively for finite graphs, and establish the finite case of the conjecture of Kwa\'sny and Stawiski whenever a distinguishing edge coloring exists. We also show that every closed locally compact permutation group with infinite motion on a countably infinite set admits continuum many inequivalent distinguishing colorings from arbitrary 2-element lists. Using compact kernels and finite bases, we extend ordinary and list equality to countable graphs with countable automorphism groups and prove that one additional list color suffices for connected locally finite graphs. Using this multiplicity and a construction fixing all vertices of infinite degree, we prove that \(D'_\ell(G)\le 2\) for every countable connected graph with infinite edge motion, settling the list infinite edge-motion conjecture of Kwa\'sny and Stawiski.
item.dc:creator: Hui Lei, Yu Wang, Yueyue Zhao

item.title: Stability and exact extremal colourings for the Alon--Frankl--Lov\'asz bound
item.description: arXiv:2611.02885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Alon--Frankl--Lov\'asz theorem states that every $q$-colouring of the edges of the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic matching of size $\lfloor(n+q-1)/(r+q-1)\rfloor$. For fixed uniformity $r$ and number of colours $q$, we prove a stability theorem: every colouring whose largest monochromatic matching has size at most $n/(r+q-1)+o(n)$ differs from a threshold extremal colouring on only $o(n^r)$ edges. We also give a necessary and sufficient structural characterization of all extremal colourings for sufficiently large $n$. The proofs combine rigidity of fractional covering weights with an extension argument for prescribed matchings. These results answer, for sufficiently large orders, the stability and extremal-colouring questions posed by Gishboliner, Glock, Michaeli and Sgueglia.
item.dc:creator: Tianhong Kan, Hongliang Lu, Feihong Yuan

item.title: On local spectra of classical distance-regular graphs with $b = 2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a combination of spectral techniques and combinatorial counts, we prove a number of non-existence results for putative distance-regular graphs with classical parameters, focusing on the case $b=2$. Among those, the case $(d,b,\alpha,\beta)=(d,2,1,2^d-2)$ passed all known feasibility conditions and required a deeper combinatorial analysis, from which nonexistence has been derived whenever $d \ge 9$. In doing so, we constructed a new family of regular graphs with four distinct eigenvalues which would have been local graphs in such a distance-regular graph.
item.dc:creator: Alexander L. Gavrilyuk, Jano\v{s} Vidali

item.title: An optimal $\chi$-bound for $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A $\textit{diamond}$ is a graph obtained by removing an edge from the complete graph on four vertices. A graph is $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-$\textit{free}$ if it contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to a seven-vertex path or a diamond. Schiermeyer (2020) asked whether there is a constant $c$ such that $\chi(G)\leq\omega(G)+c$ for every $\{P_7, \text{diamond}\}$-free graph $G$. We answer this question affirmatively by proving $\chi(G) \leq \omega(G)+3$. Moreover, the bound is optimal.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyang Lan, Hongyang Wang

item.title: Optimal Configurations for Mordell's Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mordell's problem asks for the largest product of squared pairwise distances among $n$ points in the complex plane with a prescribed sum of squared distances from the origin. When this sum equals $n$, the maximum for $2\le n\le5$ is known to be $n^n$, attained precisely by the $n$th roots of unity up to rotation and relabeling. For $n\ge6$, Chalk showed that a regular polygon together with its center gives a larger product than the regular $n$-gon. We prove that for $6\le n\le9$ the maximum is $(n-1)^{n-1}r_n^{n(n-1)}$, where $r_n=\sqrt{n/(n-1)}$. Up to the same symmetries, the unique maximizer consists of the origin and the vertices of a regular $(n-1)$-gon of radius $r_n$. For six points, algebraic elimination reduces the proof to an exact comparison of stationary values. For seven points, we compare all twelve classes in a published classification of equilibria. For eight and nine points, rigorous interval arithmetic establishes an inequality for every admissible pair. Summing over pairs gives the sharp global bound, and the equality conditions determine the configuration. An explicit ten-point comparison and a known instability result together exclude Chalk's configuration for every $n\ge10$. For each $n$ from two through eight, Mordell's problem and the minimum-diameter problem studied by Bateman and Erd\H{o}s have a common optimal configuration.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Ji, Tiancheng Xu, Wensheng Yu

item.title: Non-simple Arrangements of Lines and Pseudolines with Many Triangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.03096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study affine arrangements of an even number $n$ of lines and pseudolines with many triangles. For simple ones, Blanc's bound limits the number of triangular faces to $\lfloor n(n-5/2)/3\rfloor$. Adapting the Bartholdi-Blanc-Loisel doubling to the even case, we construct an infinite series of arrangements of $n=6\cdot2^t+2$ ($8,14,26,50,\ldots$) straight lines with two triple points and $(n(n-5/2)+1)/3$ triangles, one more than the simple bound allows. We obtain exhaustive enumerations of triangle-maximal pseudoline arrangements, simple or not, for even $n\le12$. For $n=6,8,10,12,14$ the maximum number of triangles, for both lines and pseudolines, is $7,15,25,38,54$; for $n=8,12,14$ every optimal arrangement has multiple points. All optimal arrangements for even $n\le12$ are realizable by straight lines, except two arrangements of 10 pseudolines, which are not stretchable. For the odd value $n=11$, no arrangement with $33$ triangles exists even with multiple points. We also obtain even arrangements by adding a line to odd ones. For $n\equiv2\pmod 6$ this again gives one triangle more than the simple bound, in pseudolines up to $n=44$ and in straight lines for $n=20$ and $n=32$. Doubling these pseudoline arrangements gives members of the series $18\cdot2^t+2$ and $30\cdot2^t+2$ with the same excess, up to $n=146$ and $n=242$, respectively; those with $n=38$ and $n=74$ are realizable by straight lines. These results lead us to conjecture that an arrangement of an even number $n$ of pseudolines has at most $\lfloor n(n-2)/3\rfloor-\lfloor n/6\rfloor$ triangles.
item.dc:creator: Roman Parpalak, Denis Utkin

item.title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2611.03151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 137 (2019) 112--117] asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every positive integer $m$. We answer this question negatively by constructing a graph with chromatic number and choice number $k$ that is not $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge10$. More generally, for integers $k\ge3$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$, satisfying $m>8t+\epsilon$, where $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$ is the parity of $m$, we construct such a graph that is not $(km+t:m)$-choosable. This also answers negatively the equivalent question of Xu and Zhu [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 36 (2022) 2585--2601] asking whether the strong fractional choice number of every graph is at most its choice number. This also indicates that, for each $k\ge3$, the supremum of the strong fractional choice numbers of graphs with choice number $k$ is at least $k+1/8$. When $t=0$, our construction yields counterexamples to multiplication for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge2$. In particular, it yields a $3$-choosable graph on $91$ vertices that is not $(6:2)$-choosable, answering a question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni [ Adv. Comb. (2019), Paper No. 5].
item.dc:creator: Xiaolan Hu, Jiao Li

item.title: An Erd\H{o}s-Pach-Pollack-Tuza theorem for oriented diameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.03169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The oriented diameter of a bridgeless graph is the minimum diameter of its strong orientations. Erd\H{o}s, Pach, Pollack and Tuza proved that every connected graph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta\ge 2$ has diameter at most $3n/(\delta+1)-1$, which is sharp up to an additive constant. Cochran and Wang conjectured that the oriented diameter obeys the same bound up to an absolute additive constant. We prove this conjecture: every bridgeless graph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta$ has a strong orientation of diameter at most $3n/(\delta+1)+10^{17}$. Thus the bound of Erd\H{o}s, Pach, Pollack and Tuza for the diameter carries over to the oriented diameter, with only the additive constant changed; in particular, the coefficient $3$ is best possible.
item.dc:creator: Jiangdong Ai, Bin Chen, Yaokun Feng

item.title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
item.description: arXiv:2611.03190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study weighted edge coloring, where each edge of a graph $G$ has a weight in $(0,1]$, and colors are assigned so that the incident weight of each color at every vertex is at most one. The objective is to minimize the number of colors, denoted by $\chi'_w(G)$. This generalizes classical edge coloring (all weights are one) and bin packing ($G$ is a star). Two natural lower bounds are the maximum weighted degree $\Delta_w(G)$ and the maximum local bin-packing number $\mathrm{bp}(G)$: the maximum, over vertices, of the minimum number of unit bins needed to pack the incident weights. We have $\lceil\Delta_w(G)\rceil\le\mathrm{bp}(G)\le\chi'_w(G)$. How closely these local lower bounds approximate the global optimum is a longstanding open problem. Our main result establishes an asymptotic weighted analogue of Vizing's theorem: every simple graph admits a coloring using at most $(1+o(1))\mathrm{bp}(G)$ colors. Thus local bin packings can be made globally consistent with asymptotically vanishing relative loss, even in nonbipartite graphs. Our local-to-global rounding framework coordinates feasible local packing distributions into a partial coloring, leaving only $o(\mathrm{bp}(G))$ uncolored weight at every vertex. For bipartite multigraphs, we prove $\chi'_w(G)\le(2+o(1))\Delta_w(G)$, establishing the Chung--Ross conjecture [SICOMP'91] asymptotically. For loopless multigraphs, we obtain the exact bound $\chi'_w(G)\le3\lceil\Delta_w(G)\rceil$. Both leading coefficients are optimal, giving weighted analogues of the classical K\H{o}nig--Shannon bounds. Further upper and lower bounds show that the classical factor-$3/2$ separation does not persist with the local bin-packing benchmark. We also disprove the exact weighted-degree conjecture of Feige and Singh [ESA'08]. Our upper bounds have polynomial-time algorithms, and their existence statements are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Rishikesh Gajjala, Arindam Khan

item.title: The strong fractional choice number can exceed the choice number
item.description: arXiv:2611.03236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Rubin and Taylor asked whether every $(a,b)$-choosable graph is $(am,bm)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b,m$. Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni disproved this by constructing a $4$-choosable graph that is not $(8,2)$-choosable, and asked whether a $3$-choosable graph can fail to be $(6,2)$-choosable. As a weakening, Li and Zhu asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(kb+1,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $k,b$. Equivalently, Xu and Zhu asked whether $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)\le\operatorname{ch}(G)$ for every graph $G$. Here $\operatorname{ch}(G)$ is the choice number of a graph $G$, and $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)$ is the strong fractional choice number of $G$, which is defined as the infimum of the real numbers $r$ such that $G$ is $(a,b)$-choosable for all positive integers $a,b$ with $a/b\ge r$. In this paper, we prove that, for all integers $t\ge0$ and $b\ge7t+2$, there is a planar graph $G$ with choice number three that is not $(3b+t,b)$-choosable. For $(b,t)=(2,0)$, our construction gives an affirmative answer to the question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni. This family answers the questions of Li and Zhu and of Xu and Zhu negatively, and shows that the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$ over graphs of choice number three is at least $1/7$. We further prove that, for all integers $k\ge4$, $t\ge0$ and $b\ge3t+2$, there is a graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ch}(G)=k$ that is not $(kb+t,b)$-choosable. For every $k\ge4$, this establishes the stronger lower bound $1/3$ on the supremum of $\operatorname{ch}_f^s(G)-\operatorname{ch}(G)$. The latter construction also produces simpler versions of the counterexamples of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni. It is worth mentioning that the core gadgets in both constructions are very simple. The former is an eight-vertex graph, and the latter is the six-vertex wheel $W_5$.
item.dc:creator: Yangyan Gu, Rongxing Xu

item.title: Maximizing Crossword Grids with a Fixed Minimum Clue Length
item.description: arXiv:2611.03364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an American-style crossword puzzle, the grid must be connected, 180-degree symmetric, and have minimum word length 3. Ferland and Pratt construct $n\times n$ crossword grids with many clues satisfying these conditions and prove their construction is maximal when $n\equiv 1$ or 3 $\pmod{4}$. In this paper, we explore American-style crosswords in which the minimum word length is 4. Jacobs computed the maximal $15 \times 15$ grid with minimum word length 4. In this paper, we construct grids with a maximal number of clues for all $n \not \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$.
item.dc:creator: Kelly Isham, Abigail Schnitzer

item.title: Proving the Koml\'os conjecture slowly
item.description: arXiv:2611.03427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Koml\'os conjecture was a long-standing open problem in discrepancy theory until it was recently solved in a flurry of AI developments. We give a motivated exposition of an elementary proof of the conjecture due to Karingula and Lovett, as well as a counterexample to the strong Koml\'os conjecture due to Kintali, aiming to introduce the ideas in a gentle and explained manner in order to ease the understanding of the proofs. We conclude with several problems which remain open.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence Hollom

item.title: A nearly tight bound on the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate
item.description: arXiv:2611.03444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is even-degenerate if we can order its vertices as $v_1,\dots,v_n$ so that the number of edges from $v_i$ to $v_1,\dots,v_{i-1}$ is even for all $i>2$. We show that the probability $G(n,p)$ is even-degenerate is $e^{-\Omega(n/\log\log n)}$, which is only a factor of $\log\log n$ away, in the exponent, from the trivial lower bound $2^{-O(n)}$.
item.dc:creator: Ting-Wei Chao, Bruce Reed

item.title: The proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: a detailed exposition and an extension to rotation systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.03515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number $\ucr{K_n}$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is $Z(n):=\frac{1}{4}\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\rfloor\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\rfloor$ for all $n\ge 3$. In October 2026 OpenAI uploaded to GitHub a proof of this conjecture. The proof is very short, but it relies on polynomial methods that are not part of the standard techniques used by many combinatorialists, and it is written with very little motivation or explanation. Since we found the proof very hard to follow, we decided to write this paper, which contains a complete proof of the conjecture written for mathematicians who are more familiar with combinatorics than with polynomial methods. In fact we prove a more general result on rotation systems of $K_n$, from which the Harary--Hill conjecture easily follows. Namely, we show that for every rotation system $\Pi$ of $K_n$ the number of $4$-vertex subsystems of $\Pi$ realizable as drawings of $K_4$ with one crossing, plus three times the number of non-realizable $4$-vertex subsystems of $\Pi$, is at least $Z(n)$. The statement and proof of our result are purely combinatorial and do not involve drawings at all.
item.dc:creator: Gelasio Salazar

item.title: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242
item.description: arXiv:2611.00070v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Mullet code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, and the determination of $\rho(1,9)$ is a long-standing open question. We give a computer-assisted proof that $\rho(1,9)=242$, leveraging the classification of the $349$ orbits in $\text{RM}(3,9)/\text{RM}(2,9)$ under $\text{GL}(9,2)$ [1,3]. The notebook to verify the computer search portion, Verify_RM(1,9).ipynb, contains all data and recomputes each check, and may be found in the repository https://github.com/FreemanSlaughter/Covering-Radius.
item.dc:creator: Xiang-Dong Hou, Evelyn Sabo, Freeman Slaughter

item.title: Combinatorial Algorithms for Partial Inverse Min-Max Spanning Tree Problem under the Weighted Sum Hamming Distance
item.description: arXiv:2611.00094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a connected weighted graph G=(V, E, w) and a forest F of G, the goal of partial inverse min-max spanning tree problem is to change the weight function as little as possible, so that there is a min-max spanning tree with respect to the new weight function containing F. In this paper, we study this problem under the weighted sum Hamming distance. We take the alternative set of the maximum edge weight in F with respect to the optimal weight function as a key factor, and further consider the case of this problem under the restriction of this factor. On this basis, a polynomial time algorithm with time complexity O(|V|^4) is proposed to solve this problem.
item.dc:creator: Qingzhen Dong, Xianyue Li, Xiaowen Kong

item.title: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity"
item.description: arXiv:2611.00098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rubio and Torres conjectured that a multidimensional Costas array, defined by a bijection between two boxes of integer points whose domain has at least as many dimensions as its image, can stay Costas in every window of its periodic extension only if its order is a power of two fixed by the dimension of the domain. We give a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order $6$, with a two-dimensional domain and a two-dimensional image, so the conjecture is false. The verification reduces to $36$ windows. It has been confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also meets with equality the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres use for their non-existence results, so that bound is tight.
item.dc:creator: Shiv Munagala

item.title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
item.description: arXiv:2611.00100v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. We prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and deduce the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.00156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide a counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction comes from an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. We give an explicit cardinality counterexample in $D_4^{14}$, the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order $8$.
item.dc:creator: Chandra Nair, Aref Namayandeh, Zhaobang Zhu

item.title: A new upper bound for $A(19,6,8)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00173v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute Polak's bound $A_4(19,6,8)$ for binary constant weight codes, obtaining the numerical value $673.04001$. An exact rational certificate gives $A_4(19,6,8)\le 673.0400143064802474039375132665301315202504$, and hence $A(19,6,8)\le 673$. This improves the upper bound $693$ listed in Brouwer's table. The certificate is verified by a separate program using exact rational arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Chang

item.title: Upper bounds for packings of cylinders around the unit sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.00251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note we study the problem of packing infinite circular cylinders tangent to the unit sphere. For a given number of cylinders $N$, $N\geq 3$, the maximal common cylinder radius $R_N$ is the maximum $R$ for which there exist $N$ circular cylinders of radius $R$ with non-overlapping interiors, all tangent to the unit sphere. In 1990, Kuperberg conjectured that there does not exist a packing of more than 6 cylinders of radius one tangent to the unit sphere, that is, $R_7<1$. This conjecture was recently confirmed by an exhaustive computer-assisted case analysis. Here we prove new bounds for $R_N$ for small $N$ by considering an auxiliary configuration of spherical quadrilaterals. In particular, we provide a short geometric proof of Kuperberg's conjecture and show that $R_7<0.9978$.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Glazyrin

item.title: Two moments suffice for Bessel approximation: conditioned differences, contingency tables, and probabilistic divide-and-conquer
item.description: arXiv:2611.00263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop Stein's method, with explicit constants throughout, for the discrete Bessel distribution: the law of a Poisson variable given its difference from an independent Poisson variable. The Bessel family is characterized by a birth-death operator with quadratic death rate $n(n+k)$ and as the exact fixed-point set of a centered quadratic-bias transform, and we prove a dependency expansion of Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon type: two joint moments of a column array control the total-variation distance from the conditioned row sum to a matched Bessel law. Applied to the row-constrained Fisher-Yates ensemble on $2\times c$ contingency tables -- independent Bernoulli or capped-Poisson entries conditioned on the row-sum difference, column sums free -- this yields a limit theorem -- which upgrades to the entire conditioned table at the same two-moment error -- a completely explicit enumeration estimate, and an exact divide-and-conquer sampler with certified acceptance. The entire apparatus -- operator, expansion, enumeration, sampler -- generalizes to $r\times c$ tables, where conditioning on all successive row differences produces a hyper-Bessel law. Verification scripts are included as ancillary files.
item.dc:creator: Stephen DeSalvo

item.title: Stein's method for negative binomial and hyper-negative-binomial laws, with applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.00275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop Stein's method for the negative binomial law and for the hyper-negative-binomial law, the law of the smallest row total of an array of independent geometric variables given the differences of the row totals, with every constant explicit. The main instrument is a comparison of two biasings of the approximated variable, which cancels the rate term exactly at the matched parameter. We provide total variation bounds for sums of independent geometric variables at drifting parameters, for sums of dependent geometric variables (the Arratia-Goldstein-Gordon theorem with geometric summands and the Poisson law as an endpoint), and for Poisson mixtures; the exact conditional law of negative-binomial counts given their differences, with the Bessel law as its Poisson limit; and a dependency expansion for the column direction of a contingency table. A final section verifies every bound numerically, with one script per result.
item.dc:creator: Stephen DeSalvo

item.title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus. In this paper, we give a combinatorial classification of $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in partial flag varieties. This is achieved by applying Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths forming crystal graphs of Demazure modules. Previously, Hodges and Lakshmibai classified $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in Grassmannians. $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in complete flag varieties were treated independently by Gao-Hodges-Yong and Can-Saha. Our classification generalizes and unifies these results.
item.dc:creator: Jaewon Min

item.title: A sharp plank theorem for cube annuli
item.description: arXiv:2611.00379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a conjecture of Andr\'as Bezdek on plank coverings of square annuli. A plank in a Euclidean space is the closed region between two distinct parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between them. Let $Q$ be a unit square and let $H$ be a square of side length $1/2$ whose sides are parallel to those of $Q$. Then every finite family of planks covering $Q\setminus H$ has total width at least $1$. More generally, if an axis-parallel box with side lengths $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ is removed from the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\sum_jh_j = d-1$, then every finite plank covering of the remaining set has total width at least one. The bounds are sharp.
item.dc:creator: Egor Bakaev, Alexander Polyanskii

item.title: Online carpooling against an oblivious adversary
item.description: arXiv:2611.00388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the online carpooling problem, edges on $n$ vertices arrive one at a time and must be oriented immediately, so as to keep the difference between the indegree and the outdegree of every vertex small. We give a randomized online algorithm which bounds the largest absolute difference over the first $T$ edges by $O((\log T)^{1/3})$ with high probability on every input sequence fixed in advance. This proves a conjecture of Kulkarni, Reis and Rothvoss and matches the known worst case lower bound. The algorithm keeps the law of the discrepancy vector dominated in the convex order by a Gaussian measure, and forces the endpoint with the smaller discrepancy to receive the edge whenever the two discrepancies are far apart. In the analysis we show that a vertex of discrepancy $D$ is preceded by a set of $O(D)$ vertices with total discrepancy $\Omega(D^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Lei

item.title: On the Distribution of Prime Squares and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.00485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every \(A>0\), all but \(O_A(X(\log X)^{-A})\) integers \(n<X\) satisfying \(n\equiv11\pmod{24}\) admit a representation \[ n=a^2+b^2+p^2, \] where \(p\) and \(a^2+b^2+1\) are prime and \((a,b)=1\). For ergodic averages along prime squares, we prove a universal divergence result for integrable functions, while establishing almost-everywhere convergence for near-integrable functions. We also quantify how the bounds used to establish convergence behave as one approaches integrability. Moreover, we prove endpoint improving and sparse bounds for the corresponding discrete averages, with an explicit Orlicz loss.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Mousavi

item.title: Limits and Constants of OpenAI's Claimed ETH Refutation
item.description: arXiv:2611.00517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recent OpenAI preprint claims a deterministic algorithm that counts the satisfying assignments of a $k$-CNF formula in time $2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$, and $2^{O(n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ at bounded clause density, which would refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis. The headline bound is proved by tensor contraction; the body develops an interpolation algorithm with the weaker exponent $n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n}$. This note does four things. First, it explains the interpolation algorithm in plain terms. Second, it asks how large $n$ must be for the bounds to bite. The preprint states no constants, so we treat the hidden constant $C$ as a parameter: the general bound beats the $2^n$ of brute force only beyond $n\approx 10^{32}$ for $C=2$, $10^{126}$ for $C=3$ and $10^{3517}$ for $C=10$. We then extract the constants from the tensor-contraction proof: for every input with $m$ clauses at bounded density, the running time it certifies stays above $2^n$ unless $\log_2(n+m)>10^9$, and on random 3-CNF at the satisfiability threshold unless $\log_2 n>5\times10^{11}$. So the bounds are subexponential as $n\to\infty$, but the proof certifies no speed-up over brute force for any input of bounded density that could ever be written down. Third, for the clause-product form of the interpolation algorithm we prove limits in a cost model matching the preprint's evaluation. By a short algebraic lemma, polynomial cost needs components of $O(\log^3 n)$ variables with per-point evaluation, or primal treewidth $O(\log^2 n)$ with dynamic programming over the groups. So the scheme costs $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\mathrm{tw}})}$ at treewidth $\mathrm{tw}$, $2^{\Omega(\sqrt n)}$ with high probability on random 3-CNF above clause density 3, and $2^{\Omega(n^{1/3})}$ even on trivially countable path formulas. We explain why the preprint's sharper routes escape these limits. Fourth, we report experiments.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Dias, Yvens Lima

item.title: On Certain Congruences for Partition $k$-Tuples with $5$-Cores
item.description: arXiv:2611.00693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of partition $k$-tuples of $n$ with $t$-cores. Using fifth-order modular equations and the Atkin $U_5$-operator, we prove the congruences $A_{5,125i+21}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{9,14,19,24\}$, $A_{5,125i+41}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{19,24\}$, and $A_{5,125i+111}(125n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^4}$ for $r\in\{39,64,89,114\}$, which were stated by Tang \cite{tang2025iterative}.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Maity

item.title: CLT for the Weight of the Minimum Spanning Arborescence on the Complete Directed Graph
item.description: arXiv:2611.00698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The minimum spanning arborescence (MSA) with a fixed boundary, defined on weighted directed graphs, is the directed analogue of the minimum spanning tree (MST). The behaviour of the MSA has been of recent interest and is known to be quite different from that of its undirected counterpart. On the complete directed graph, and for edge weights given by i.i.d. random variables with a broad class of distributions, we prove a Central Limit Theorem for the weight of the MSA with appropriate scaling. While the scaling for the CLT is similar to MST case explored by Janson, the centering required ($1$ as opposed to $\zeta(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) and the limiting variance of the Gaussian ($1$ as opposed to $6\zeta(4)-4\zeta(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) are notably different.
item.dc:creator: Swarnadeep Bagchi, Pablo de la Fuente, Kesav Krishnan

item.title: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.00728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.
item.dc:creator: Koustav Banerjee, Kathrin Bringmann

item.title: A result of continuous stability for generalized persistence diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2611.00799v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study persistence modules obtained from the $A$-fundamental groupoids of finite graphs. Moreover, we verify the categorical properties needed to form generalized persistence diagrams, and describe a quotient that identifies equivalent groupoids. A normalized linear presheaf construction places these modules in an essentially small abelian category, where Patel's Continuity Theorem gives a $1$-Lipschitz estimate in erosion distance. Explicit graph filtrations illustrate the groupoid-valued construction, and so we suggest a new approach to interpret persistence diagrams and large data sets in topological data analysis, based on recent works of A-homotopy theory of the last years.
item.dc:creator: Yanga Bavuma, Martin Mijangos, Francesco G. Russo

item.title: Well begun is half done: the computation of Eulerian paths
item.description: arXiv:2611.00818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize the uniform computational strength of finding one-way Eulerian paths in countable graphs. For both directed and undirected graphs, this problem is Weihrauch-equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}\times\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ is the jump of closed choice on the natural numbers. This refines the proof-theoretical strength of the existence of an Eulerian path given by the reverse mathematics framework. The $\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}'$ component comes entirely from the difficulty of choosing a starting vertex: with a valid start prescribed, the problem is equivalent to $\mathsf{lim}$. We also study the problem $\mathsf{OrientEP}$ of orienting an undirected graph while preserving the existence of a one-way Eulerian path. We prove $\mathsf{lim}_2<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{OrientEP}<_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{2}'\sqcap\mathsf{Sort}_2$ and $\mathsf{OrientEP}\not\le_{\mathrm{W}}\mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$.
item.dc:creator: Manlio Valenti

item.title: Identities for generalized Bernoulli numbers from a Lie model of the 2-disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.00825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define generalized Bernoulli numbers as appropriate coefficients of the Baker--Campbell--Hausdorff (BCH) product formula, extending the classical sequence of rational numbers to a 2-dimensional setting. We give an identity involving these numbers and the classical Bernoulli numbers which is equivalent to the existence of a particular complete differential graded Lie algebra modelling a cell decomposition of the 2-disk and based on the Lawrence--Sullivan model of the interval. From this identity we derive explicit quadratic relations. The existence of Lie models for the symmetries of the interval and the disk is related to certain properties of the BCH product and to some notable features of the classical Bernoulli numbers: the two choices for $B_1$, the vanishing of $B_n$ for odd $n\geq 3$, and the equality $B_4=B_8$.
item.dc:creator: Urtzi Buijs, Jos\'e Manuel Moreno Fern\'andez

item.title: Regions of totally real arrangements of rational curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.00861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a plane-curve analogue of Zaslavsky's theorem for arrangements of real rational curves for which every complex singularity with more than one local branch is real and all of its branches are real. If at least one component has odd degree, the number of real regions equals the total rational Betti number of the complexified complement. We also give a formula for bounded affine regions which records the number of branches at infinity and the connected components of the real affine curve. Oriented regions generate the middle Borel--Moore homology over $\mathbb{Q}$, and they generate it over $\mathbb{Z}$ when the component degrees are coprime. The relations are described by the circles in the real normalization and, in an affine chart, by winding functions. These results imply equality of combinatorial rank and real combinatorial rank in the framework of Brown--Dupont and Sturmfels--Telen. Examples include singular rational cubics, arrangements of conics, Chebyshev curves, and the plane model of the $27$ lines on a split cubic surface.
item.dc:creator: Masahiko Yoshinaga

item.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.00864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.
item.dc:creator: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu

item.title: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242
item.description: arXiv:2611.00890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242. Equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of a Boolean function in nine variables is 242. Our proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with a spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. We first show that every nine-variable Boolean function of nonlinearity 243 admits a unique one-point modification that raises its nonlinearity to 244: the point to be changed is the vector sum of its support. This part uses exact Walsh-update identities, integer interpolation, rigidity of a quadratic residue, and a sharp Walsh l1 estimate for cubic Boolean functions. To exclude nonlinearity 244, we use Parseval's identity and congruences of integral Walsh coefficients to force an exceptionally restricted spectrum. An associated cubic residue phase must attain the extremal Walsh l1 bound 10240. We eliminate one equality spectrum by hyperplane slicing; the other forces the original Boolean function from the signs of the cubic phase and yields a double-complement-pairing identity for its cubic top part. The classification of alternating trilinear forms over F2, an exact filter of their representatives, and two exhaustive enumerations of 218 quadratic supplements then rule out every remaining candidate. Together with the known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the asserted covering radius.
item.dc:creator: Yi Li

item.title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.00925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime $p$, the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic $p$ have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to $p$, every such code over every finite field of characteristic $p$ has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled by Moree.
item.dc:creator: Tao Feng, Henk D. L. Hollmann, Weicong Li, Qing Xiang

item.title: Linear resolutions of powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs with matching number four
item.description: arXiv:2611.00961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a finite simple gap-free graph $G$, let $B(G)$ denote the vertices $v$ for which $G-N_G[v]$ is not co-chordal, and put $C(G)=V(G)\setminus B(G)$. We prove a sufficient condition for all ordinary powers of its edge ideal to have linear resolutions from the second power onward: every induced anticycle of length at least five must contain an edge with both endpoints in $C(G)$. The argument uses variable generators of augmented colon ideals to eliminate anticycles that may persist in the ordinary quadratic colons. It yields linear resolutions for all powers $I(G)^q$, $q\ge2$, whenever the ordinary matching number is at most four, which answers the first part of a question of Erey, H\`a, Hibi, Kara and Morey. The criterion also applies to certain graphs with adjacent exceptional vertices and matching number five. The proofs are theoretical and valid over arbitrary fields. We do not assert linear quotients.
item.dc:creator: Luis Alfredo Dupont Garc\'ia

item.title: Mutual-visibility colouring with two colours is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
item.description: arXiv:2611.01012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A mutual-visibility set in a graph $G$ is a set $S$ of vertices such that any two vertices of $S$ are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition $V(G)$. Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter $d$, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. The proof rests on a reformulation of $\chi_\mu(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the $2$-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from $2$-colourability of $3$-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.
item.dc:creator: Siddhesh Chaubal

item.title: Maximal input entropy for binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.01064v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under uniform transmission, we determine the received binary words that maximize input entropy for two-deletion and two-insertion channels. For two deletions the maximizers are exactly the two alternating words at every positive received length. For two insertions the same conclusion holds from received length five onward; we give all smaller cases and exact maximal values. The proof combines an embedding-count identity organized by runs with strict convexity estimates, and a grouping of two-position deletion masks. For every insertion radius we give the complete positive embedding histogram of an alternating received word. We also determine its three-deletion histogram for every length, and certify all three-deletion maximizers through received length twelve and all three-insertion maximizers through length eighteen by exact integer comparison. These computations give precise three-error conjectures with their small-length exceptions.
item.dc:creator: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: On Sparse Graph Limits for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph neural networks are often trained on small graphs and deployed on larger ones, raising the question of which graph information must be preserved for combinatorial optimization values to transfer across sizes. We establish size-transfer guarantees for normalized graph optimization values using finite collections of energy features. For affine objectives, including MAX-CUT, coloring defect, and independent-set density, differences in task value are controlled by discrepancies in normalized scalar energy probes on all bounded-degree graphs. For general Lipschitz objectives, such as those with balance penalties, an additional representation error appears; this error vanishes on hyperfinite graph families but can remain bounded away from zero on expanders. Thus, at fixed degree bound, state space, Lipschitz constant, and target accuracy, a finite energy representation independent of graph size suffices universally for affine tasks and asymptotically for general Lipschitz tasks on hyperfinite families. These results yield prediction guarantees under explicit conditions on encoder accuracy, readout stability, and representation coverage, together with statistical generalization bounds. Theoretically, we prove Shapley-Folkman bounds with sharp parameter dependence, including a dimension-free $\ell_2$ regime, and realize the resulting energy features with a fixed-weight message-passing network using random node initialization on bounded-treewidth graphs. Experiments with exact solvers and trained models test the resulting transfer guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Thien Le, Melanie Weber

item.title: The Value of Steiner Hubs in Two-Hop Distance Labeling
item.description: arXiv:2611.01106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two-hop distance labelings were introduced in 2002 by Cohen, Halperin, Kaplan, and Zwick with hubs of two kinds: vertices of the graph, or, in their Steiner variant, arbitrary objects carrying arbitrary real values. On no family is the value of that freedom known. We determine it on $\ell_1$ products of betweenness-free metrics, those with no point between two others, a class containing every Hamming graph. The freedom is worth nothing when the factors have at most three letters, while from four letters on the largest saving is polynomial in the size of the product, attained on products of positively weighted stars. The $d$-dimensional hypercube is the two-letter case, and labeling it takes $(5/2+o(1))^d$ entries even with arbitrary hubs, matching the vertex-hub optimum of Goldberg, Razenshteyn, and Savchenko. Every lower bound here comes from one semidefinite program on a single factor, whose value $\Lambda$ never exceeds the rate that vertex hubs already achieve on the Hamming graph; where $\Lambda$ meets that ceiling, the freedom is worth nothing, and the ceiling is met exactly up to three letters.
item.dc:creator: Sichen Wang

item.title: Fluid Limits and Upper Bounds for Randomized Greedy Matching
item.description: arXiv:2611.01177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Modified Randomized Greedy (MRG) algorithm [Tinhofer (1984), Aronson-Dyer-Frieze-Suen (1995)] is a classical greedy algorithm for finding approximate maximum matchings. MRG repeatedly picks a uniformly random unmatched vertex and matches it to a uniformly random unmatched neighbor, if one exists. Since 1991, the best upper bound on its approximation ratio has been $2/3$, given by the Bomb graphs of [Dyer and Frieze (1991)]. We improve this bound to $0.6569$ on general graphs and $0.6607$ on bipartite graphs. Our constructions consist of copies of small gadgets, with specified vertex classes joined completely. We track each algorithm by counting gadget copies with each possible configuration of remaining vertices. Wormald's differential equation method [Wormald (1995)] shows that these counts, scaled by the size parameter of the construction, converge to a deterministic trajectory known as the \textit{fluid limit}, which is described by ordinary differential equations. This fluid limit approximation holds while the relevant vertex classes have positive density, and so we devise a separate counting argument determines the contribution from the end of the run. Furthermore, we apply our framework to Random Decision Order (RDO), in which vertices are processed in uniformly random order and choose unmatched neighbors according to fixed adversarial preferences. On bipartite graphs, we determine the exact limiting ratio on the Double-Bomb family of [Tang-Wu-Zhang (2020)]. Its minimum is $31/48$, confirming their numerical estimate of about $0.646$.On general graphs, we improve their upper bound of $5/8$, given by the paw graph, to $0.5946$ on a new family. Finally, we give one possible explanation for why $2/3$ seemed to be optimal for MRG in the concluding remarks.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Mukherjee

item.title: An $\mathsf{FPRAS}$ for Mixed Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We design the first fully polynomial-time randomized approximation scheme ($\mathsf{FPRAS}$) to estimate the mixed volume of $n$ arbitrary compact convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ specified by weak membership oracles. This disproves a longstanding conjecture of Gurvits (2009). $\textbf{AI Disclosure}$ The main ideas were generated entirely by GPT 6 Astra. The purpose of this paper is to provide a human-written exposition of the algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu

item.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
item.description: arXiv:2611.01422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.
item.dc:creator: Olga Holtz

item.title: A log-concavity criterion for finite nonnegative linearization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a 2005 survey, R. Szwarc asked for criteria, stated in the recurrence coefficients, for nonnegative linearization (property (P)) of finite orthogonal polynomial systems such as the Krawtchouk polynomials. For a finite three-term recurrence normalized to have row sums one, whose diagonal and downward coefficients have a constant nonnegative ratio, we prove that property (P) holds for every product, including products beyond the terminal degree, whenever the Newton coefficients of the profile $d_i=b_i+c_i$ are log-concave without internal zeros. The criterion contains the full positive Krawtchouk range and the dual $q$-Krawtchouk arrays, and through a quadratic decomposition of symmetric finite systems it covers Szwarc's quadratic system $Q_n$ in its sharp range $0<p_0\leq1/2$. As a limit to any such criterion, property (P) fails at coefficient distance $O((1-r^2)^N)$ from the Krawtchouk array of size $N$ with fixed ratio $c_i/d_i=r<1$. All theorems, corollaries and propositions are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Leslie P. Polzer

item.title: Dimension bounds for finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most $81$, substantially improving Prokhorov's bound of $995$. A refinement of Prokhorov's method gives the intermediate bound $162$, while an extension of Vinberg's planar-angle comparison to the finite-volume setting yields the sharper bound. Both arguments combine improved weighting functions with estimates using cusp geometry to control weight contributions of angles at ideal vertices or edges incident to them.
item.dc:creator: Lizi Guo, Fangting Zheng

item.title: Approximation Algorithms for Maximum-Weight Degree-Bounded Forests
item.description: arXiv:2611.01875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem, we are given a graph with nonnegative edge weights and a degree upper bound on each vertex. The objective is to find a maximum-weight forest satisfying the degree bounds. We show that this problem admits a simple $2$-approximation via the greedy algorithm. This already improves over the best-known guarantees obtained via a reduction to weighted $3$-matroid parity, and sets a baseline to improve upon. Our main result is an $\frac{8}{5}$-approximation algorithm for the maximum-weight degree-bounded forest problem. For the special case of uniform degree bounds, our algorithm achieves an approximation ratio of $\frac{3}{2}$. It computes two sets of edges, each of which we then restrict to a feasible solution in an optimal way, and finally returns the better of the two resulting solutions. To obtain the initial two edge sets, we first relax the degree bounds and leverage an algorithm by Lau and Singh [JACM'15] for degree-bounded spanning trees, and second we relax the forest constraints and employ an algorithm for maximum-weight $b$-matchings.
item.dc:creator: Theophile Thiery, Vera Traub, Nicola Widmer

item.title: Optimal asymptotic bounds for design curves on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A spherical $t$-design is a finite set of points on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere such that averaging any polynomial of degree at most $t$ over these points gives its exact spherical average. We study the corresponding notion for curves, where point averages are replaced by normalized arclength integration. For fixed $d\ge 2$, the length of such curves is known to be bounded below by a positive multiple of $t^{d-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. We show that this asymptotic order is attained: for every $d\ge 2$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that, for every positive integer $t$ and every prescribed length $L\ge C_dt^{d-1}$, there is a simple spherical $t$-design curve of length $L$. This establishes the analogue for curves of the theorem of Bondarenko, Radchenko, and Viazovska, which resolved the Korevaar-Meyers conjecture for spherical design points. More generally, we prove the corresponding result on closed, connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension $d\ge 2$, where eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator substitute for polynomials. The proof combines a geometric construction of curves with continuously adjustable local lengths and an application of Brouwer's degree theorem.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ehler

item.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
item.description: arXiv:2611.01906v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give explicit kissing configurations in R^d for every d = 49, ..., 61. The lower bound is improved over the best previously published value in all thirteen dimensions, by margins from 232 to 159,220 points and by 506,461 points in total. The configurations are obtained from the antipodal block lift of Yang et al. applied to the 52,416,000-point minimal shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p, using a class of 7,193 minimal lines and, in each dimension, a kissing configuration of R^k (k <= 15) with the largest available number of antipodal pairs. Two ingredients are new. The published class of 7,077 lines is grown to 7,193 by local search in three stages, as a sequence of exchanges between candidate lines and class lines; and the point count, which equals 52,416,000 + 2S + 2t with t the number of antipodal pairs and S the size of the union of t isometric images of the class, is maximised as a maximum-coverage problem by greedy search with iterated local search over pools of 4,000 automorphic images, reaching 92-100% of the trivial bound 7,193t. All results are verified in exact integer arithmetic, and the certificates are distributed with the code. Code and data: https://github.com/dimkadimon/KissingNumbers
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Kamenetsky

item.title: Theoretical relations between basic centrality measures in real-world networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.01957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish new relationships among several fundamental measures of real-world networks, including the average clustering coefficient, the global clustering coefficient, the average shortest-path length and degree centrality, closeness centrality, betweenness centrality and ksi-centrality. We further develop the theory of $j$-neighborhood centrality, which encompasses degree centrality and ksi-centrality as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Tuzhilin

item.title: Volume Doubling and Geometric Inequalities on Graphs with Bakry-\'Emery Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.02010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider irreducible reversible Markov chains whose nonzero off-diagonal transition probabilities are bounded below by $\epsilon>0$ and whose reversible measure satisfies $m_-\le m(x)\le\kappa m_-$. Under the Bakry--\'Emery curvature condition $\mathrm{CD}(K,\infty)$, with $K\in\mathbb{R}$, we establish Wang's log-Harnack inequality $$ P_t(\log f)(x)\le\log P_tf(y) +\frac{C\mathrm{dist}(x,y)^2}{\int_0^t e^{2Ks}\mathrm{d} s}, $$ for bounded positive $f$ bounded away from zero and all $x,y\in V$, where $C$ is a constant dependent only on $\varepsilon$. Building upon this inequality, we further prove volume doubling property: let $K_-:=\max\{-K,0\}$ $$ \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,2R))\le C_0\exp\!\bigl(C_1\sqrt{K_-}\,R\bigr) \mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R)),\qquad R>0, $$ where $C_0,C_1$ depend only on $\epsilon,\kappa$. If $d$ is the maximum combinatorial degree of the support graph, we further prove under $\mathrm{CD}(0,\infty)$ the sharp volume growth bound $\mathrm{Vol}(B(o,R))\le m_-CR^{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}$ for all $o$ and $R\geq 1$.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Ding, Shiping Liu, Chiyu Zhou

item.title: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.02167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features. Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vec{\lambda}:=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $\lambda_1\neq \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_3\neq \lambda_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vec{\lambda}} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-\lambda_1 t)\,f_2(x-\lambda_2 t-\lambda_3 t^a)\,f_3(x-\lambda_4 t^a)\,\frac{dt}{t},\quad x \in \mathbb{R}\,.$$ By combining variable multiresolution, multiscale wave-packet analysis, and Rank II LGC method, our present work establishes a common framework where the diverse methodologies of all of the following naturally converge: i) the maximal truncated bilinear Hilbert transform, ii) the Biest operator, iii) the hybrid bilinear Hilbert-Carleson operator, and iv) the non-resonant (curved) trilinear Hilbert transform. Ultimately, this work reveals that the hybrid trilinear transform sits on a critical intermediate scale between the purely non-resonant case and the purely resonant regime -- the latter remaining a challenging, major (open) problem in harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Cristina Benea, Fr\'ed\'eric Bernicot, Victor Lie

item.title: Minimal cellular resolutions of complementary edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.02168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an explicit minimal cellular resolution for every squarefree monomial ideal generated in degree $n-2$ in the polynomial ring $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$. Such an ideal is the complementary edge ideal $I_c(G)$ of a simple graph $G$ on $[n]$, and the resolution is supported on a labeled regular CW complex $X_G$ of dimension at most $2$. This yields closed formulas for the differentials and for the multigraded Betti numbers of $I_c(G)$ in terms of graph invariants. We then determine the $a$-invariant of $S/I_c(G)$ in terms of the vertex connectivity of $G$. Finally, when $S/I_c(G)$ is Cohen--Macaulay, we describe the canonical module and its Hilbert series, and recover the known characterizations of the Gorenstein and level cases.
item.dc:creator: Somayeh Moradi

item.title: An $L\log L$ theory of sparse graph convergence
item.description: arXiv:2611.02187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Borgs, Chayes, Cohn and Zhao developed a limit theory for sparse graphs based on $L^p$ upper regularity with $p>1$, where Holder's inequality controls small sets. We develop the analogous theory in the Orlicz class $L\log L$, replacing Holder by the Young-Fenchel inequality for $\Psi(u)=(1+u)\log(1+u)-u$ and $\Psi^*(v)=e^v-1-v$. We prove a weak regularity lemma for upper $\Psi$-regular graphons with $4^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts, using the modular $\int\Psi$ as the energy; that upper $\Psi$-regular sequences have cut-metric convergent subsequences; that convergent sequences with $L\log L$ limits are upper $\Psi$-regular; and that $L\log L$ balls are cut-metric compact. The class strictly contains every $L^p$ class with $p>1$, and we give sparse $W$-random graphs that are upper $\Psi$-regular but not upper $L^p$ regular for any $p>1$. For graphs with a given degree sequence we prove, by Stein's method of exchangeable pairs with switchings, that if the average degree tends to infinity, the density to zero and the degree profile converges in $L^1$ to $\varphi$, uniformly random graphs converge in the normalized cut metric to $\varphi\otimes\varphi$, with no condition on the maximum degree; the sequence is upper $\Psi$-regular when $\varphi\in L\log L$. We also show that the maximum-entropy $\beta$-model is entrywise Chung-Lu when $d_{\max}^2=o(M)$, and that cut-closeness to it follows from a lower bound $e^{-o(M)}$ on its probability of having the prescribed degrees.
