Finally, $\Psi$ is the large deviation rate function of sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs up to a factor $1+O(1/\log\frac1p)$.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Mehrdad

item.title: Around the Clock. New Twists on Fitch Cheney's Five-Card Trick
item.description: arXiv:2611.02424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fitch Cheney's five-card trick is one of the purest two-person effects in card magic, and it has attracted mathematicians for more than seventy five years. This article retells the effect and its classic method, surveys how far it can be pushed, and presents several new results that matter to performers. We give a version of Cheney's method that needs no fixed first suit and no fixed ``lowest card'': shifting every card one step in rank and one step in suit shifts the display in the same way. A heckler who may swap two neighboring cards of the display defeats every method with a full deck. We show that a 29-card deck is the largest for which such a swap can be corrected, and that the corresponding maximum is 14 cards if any two cards may be swapped. We give simple methods that achieve both bounds. Finally, we make Berlekamp's arithmetic method for the 124-card deck independent of where the numbering starts. We also describe a pocket version with eight cards.
item.dc:creator: Doron Levy, Yaakov Malinovsky

item.title: Large independent sets via neighborhood block dynamics, Glauber dynamics, and local occupancy
item.description: arXiv:2611.02483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local occupancy can be used to bound the expected size of a hard-core independent set. The framework of locally stationary distributions shows that for triangle-free graphs, despite slow mixing at the relevant fugacity parameter, standard Glauber dynamics can be used to find sets close to the local occupancy guarantee. We improve the application of this framework to the hard-core model by replacing a conditional mixing argument with a more direct approach based on a short sequence of single-site updates that, from every initial configuration, achieves the required occupancy inequality. In general graphs, naive conditional mixing estimates or certain problematic structures in the neighborhood can in principle incur running time cost exponential in the maximum degree $\Delta$. We design short update sequences that, via our relaxed criterion, yield running times polynomial in $\Delta$ for graphs with a hereditary bound $b$ on the density of $K_{t,t}$ subgraphs in neighborhoods. Our methods handle the case where $t$ and $b$ can grow with the maximum degree, and the resulting algorithm attains the random graph shattering threshold when they grow sufficiently slowly. That is, we give improved local occupancy parameters and a short update sequence analysis which together show that Glauber dynamics finds independent sets of size $(1-o(1))n(\log\Delta)/\Delta$ in time polynomial in $n$ and $\Delta$ whenever $t$ and $b$ are constant or grow suitably slowly. In a similar regime, we also establish that the (correspondence) chromatic number is at most $(1+o(1))\Delta/\log\Delta$ which improves upon prior results by a factor of at least $4$ in the case $t\ge 4$.
item.dc:creator: Ewan Davies, Brian Tan

item.title: Counterexamples to a Cubic Nondegeneracy Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.02544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko conjectured that a cubic Boolean generating function satisfying an ordered separation condition on its second polar must be equivalent to one of two symmetric normal forms. Two infinite families of counterexamples are constructed and proved analytically; both are direct sums of small seeds, and neither is equivalent to the proposed forms even after linear functions are added. The first adjoins a nondegenerate quadratic block to a ternary cubic seed and is distinguished from the proposed forms by the radical of its third polar. This radical determines the associative nucleus of every twisted quasialgebra with the given generating function, so the corresponding algebras are not isomorphic even when the grading is forgotten. The second family consists of direct sums of a five-variable seed and has zero third-polar radical. A criterion for quadratic-block presentations establishes the separation property of the seed; commutation-graph degrees, radical dimensions, and contraction ranks establish non-equivalence in all dimensions of the family.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Pineda Montoya

item.title: Generalized parabolic Demazure modules and the N!/2-conjecture for two-row diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2611.02749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a family of generalized parabolic Demazure modules, i.e. of gl[x]-submodules of tensor products of integrable representations of the affine Lie algebra generated by tensor products of extremal vectors, and describe these modules by generators and relations. Realizing the Garsia--Haiman modules of two-row diagrams as fusion products of two local Weyl modules, we show that their y-graded components admit filtrations whose associated graded modules are isomorphic to tensor products of these generalized parabolic Demazure modules with the cohomology rings of Grassmannians. As a consequence, the Garsia-Haiman modules of two-row diagrams of a fixed size generate a distributive lattice, and the N!/2-conjecture holds for two-row diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Anton Khoroshkin, Ievgen Makedonskyi

item.title: Closed energy formulas on tensor squares of perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each integer $l\ge1$, we give closed formulas for the local energies on tensor squares of the level-$l$ perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$, normalized to vanish at the all-zero coordinate tensors. The $D_4^{(3)}$ energy is the maximum of three defects, equivalently of nine linear forms in parameters of classical highest-weight elements. Eliminating these parameters yields the maximum of nine piecewise-linear functions of the twelve input coordinates. Tensor-compatible similarity identifies the $G_2^{(1)}$ energy at level $l$ with one third of the pullback of the $D_4^{(3)}$ energy at level $3l$, yielding the same coordinate formula. The formula has no explicit level dependence, respects natural coordinate-set inclusions between levels, and allows direct evaluation without the combinatorial $R$-matrix or crystal-graph traversal.
item.dc:creator: Shaolong Han

item.title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.02795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,\alpha,\beta,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{\lambda_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $\alpha/N$ and $\beta/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}\chi_\lambda(x)\,\Delta^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^\beta (x_a-p)^\alpha\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.
item.dc:creator: Matvey Sushkov

item.title: Buildings governed by twisted Bruhat orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.02925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper introduces the notion of a twisted building associated to a Coxeter system and an initial section of a reflection order. These are pairs of buildings and a map between them which depends on a twisted Bruhat order. It is proved that projection maps exist between components and that the common apartment property holds for a suitable notion of an apartment, generalising what is known for twin buildings. Several well-known examples are given, including a family of twisted buildings associated to an affine building and its fa\c{c}ades.
item.dc:creator: Harvey Sykes

item.title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
item.description: arXiv:2611.02963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(\Omega(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.
item.dc:creator: Yali Aharon-Holzman, Michael Ilan, Assaf Reiner, Amnon Ta-Shma

item.title: Reed-Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
item.description: arXiv:2611.03145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that any linear $3$-query locally correctable code $C \colon \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with constant correction radius must have length $n \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{k})}$. This improves on the prior best lower bound of $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{k/\log k})}$, due to [AG24], and shows that the folklore construction of linear $3$-LCCs from Reed-Muller codes, which achieve length $n = 2^{O(\sqrt{k})}$, is optimal up to constant factors in the exponent. Our proof builds on the approach of [KM24a], further refined in [Yan24,KM24b], that uses "chain derived equations" in combination with Kikuchi graphs. The crux of our argument is to show that a certain edge-coloured Kikuchi graph has a unique colour cycle: a cycle in which some colour is used exactly once. We do this by controlling the distribution of colours at each vertex in the graph using a random walk mixing argument and a novel hypergraph decomposition based on edge expansion of the hypergraph's "flattening" into a graph.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Janzer, Peter Manohar

item.title: Exact Agreement Expansion up to the Top via Non-polarity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agreement expansion asks whether local assignments to faces of a poset that usually agree on a sampled common face must agree with a single global function on most faces. Agreement expansion is exact (approximate) if local assignments need to exactly (approximately) agree with the global function. We suggest a new proof technique for agreement expansion that enables agreement expansion in settings which were previously beyond reach, such as: exact agreement expansion for Grassmannian posets (before only simplicial complexes support exact agreement expansion); agreement expansion based on assignments to top faces of the a complex (before agreement expansion is generally proven only for assignments to low dimensional faces); agreement expansion from one-sided spectral expansion (before, two sided spectral assumption was needed in general settings). Specifically, for down-closed simplicial and Grassmannian complexes, we prove an exact agreement theorem between any two layers assuming one-sided spectral expansion in links of singletons. As an application, we show that full bases of every rank-$k$ matroid admit exact agreement with soundness $O(k^2/[h(k-h)])$ when tested through $h$-element independent sets. We also obtain exact agreement on Grassmannian posets under one-sided spectral expansion, with stronger soundness under a local distance guarantee. Our key proof ideas center around non-polarity of the distributions of local assignments, probed via a random exposure of elements.
item.dc:creator: Tali Kaufman, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: Finite groups with all involutions fused
item.description: arXiv:2611.03366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize finite groups whose involutions form a single fusion class. In the solvable case, we show that the $2$-length is $1$, extending Thompson's theorem which states that a solvable group with all involutions conjugate has $2$-length $1$. For a nonsolvable group $G$, we prove that if its involutions are fused then they are conjugate; moreover, $G/\mathbf{O}_{2'}(G)$ is almost quasisimple. As an application, we obtain a restriction on $m$ for which an $m$-pyramidal Kirkman triple system can be realized under a nonsolvable group.
item.dc:creator: Zheng Guo, Yan Zhou Zhu

item.title: Centralizers of maps as automorphism groups of Yang--Baxter solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03380v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a partition $X = Y \sqcup Z$ of a set $X$ and an arbitrary map $g \colon Y \to {\rm Hom}_{\rm Set} (Z, \, Z)$, we construct a solution $R_g \colon X \times X \to X \times X$ of the braid equation. We characterize intrinsically the solutions which are isomorphic to some $R_g$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for two solutions $R_g$ and $R_{g'}$ to be isomorphic. Consequently, the number of isomorphism classes of the solutions $R_g$ on a set with $n$ elements is $1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{n-1} \widetilde{o} (n - k, \, k)$, where $\widetilde{o} (m, \, k)$ is the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$, acting by conjugation, on the set of multisets with $k$ elements of maps $\{1, \ldots, m\} \to \{1, \ldots, m\}$. This construction is then used to obtain a solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is exactly the centralizer ${\rm Aut} (f_1, \ldots, f_k)$ of a given family $f_1, \ldots, f_k \colon X \to X$ of maps, $k \geq 1$. For $k = 2$, combined with a result of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, this gives another proof of the fact that any group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a solution of the braid equation (equivalently, of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation).
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: The Optimizer's Windfall: Bounding Hindsight Gain under Random Restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Suppose an optimization problem is randomly restricted, independently on each variable, and re-optimized after the restriction is revealed. For multilinear objectives, every fixed solution is unbiased after rescaling, but re-optimizing introduces an upward bias. We bound this excess, the hindsight gain, over products of arbitrary compact local domains in Euclidean unit balls. For interactions $A=(A_e)_e$ among $r$ distinct variables and independent random weights $\zeta_i$, the gain is at most $O_r(\|A\|_F M^{(r-1)/2}\sigma_{\max})$, where $\|A\|_F^2$ is the sum of squared coefficients, $M=\sum_i\mathbb{E}\zeta_i^2$, and $\sigma_{\max}^2=\max_i\mathrm{Var}(\zeta_i)$; only second moments are needed. Under uniform retention with probability $p$, we sharpen this to $O_r(p^{r-1/2}\sqrt{1-p}\,n^{(r-1)/2}\|A\|_F)$, which is tight for every fixed $r$ and $p\in(0,1)$. Our proof combines a comparison principle along a single support direction with tensor projection, vector contraction, and repeated thinning. Applications: (i) For fixed arity and alphabet size, solving the subproblem induced by $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ sampled variables estimates a dense Max-$r$CSP optimum within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, and this sample size is optimal. (ii) The same approach estimates MaxCut and the distance to bipartiteness within $\pm\varepsilon n^2$ using $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ nonadaptive queries and $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ examined vertices, both optimal. (iii) We answer a question of Yufei Zhao: vertex percolation at rate $p$ preserves the max-cut fraction whenever $p\,e(G)/v(G)\to\infty$, and this condition is sharp. (iv) For bounded $r$-local quantum Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ uniformly sampled particles suffice to estimate the ground-state energy within $\pm\varepsilon n^r$, improving the previous $O(\varepsilon^{-6}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bound.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohui Bei, Wenhao Wu

item.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.03578v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka

item.title: On ill-distributed $B_3$ and $B_4$ sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03609v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, for $k\in\{3,4\}$, a $B_k$-set $A\subseteq[N]$ has size $o(N^{1/k})$ if it omits a fixed positive proportion of the residue classes modulo every prime in a fixed family whose reciprocals have divergent sum.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Hisatsuga, Rafael Miyazaki, Cosmin Pohoata

item.title: Get Permanent Results Faster by Counting Stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.03636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that $n \times n$ permanents can be computed with $O^*{(2-\varepsilon)^n}$ arithmetic operations over every commutative ring, for $\varepsilon = 10^{-40}$. This solves a problem stated in Knuth's The Art of Computer Programming. Our algorithm implements the classical Binet--Minc identity with dynamic programming and careful bookkeeping. It also gives algebraic branching programs of size $O^*{(2-\varepsilon)^n}$.
item.dc:creator: Radu Curticapean

item.title: High order free hyperplane arrangements in 3-dimensional vector spaces
item.description: arXiv:1903.03249v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Holm introduced $m$-free $\ell$-arrangements which is a generalization of free arrangements, while he asked whether all $\ell$-arrangements are $m$-free for $m$ large enough. Recently Abe and the author verified that this question is in the negative when $\ell\geq 4$. In this paper we verify that $3$-arrangements $\mathscr{A}$ are $m$-free and compute the $m$-exponents for all $m\geq |\mathscr{A}|+2$, where $|\mathscr{A}|$ is the cardinality of $\mathscr{A}$. Hence Holm's question is in the positive when $\ell=3$. Finally we prove that $3$-dimensional Weyl arrangements of types A and B are $m$-free for all $m\geq 0$.
item.dc:creator: Norihiro Nakashima

item.title: An inverse theorem for Freiman multi-homomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2002.11667v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G_1, \dots, G_k$ and $H$ be vector spaces over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_p$ of prime order. Let $A \subset G_1 \times\dots\times G_k$ be a set of size $\delta |G_1| \cdots |G_k|$. Let a map $\phi \colon A \to H$ be a multi-homomorphism, meaning that for each direction $d \in [k]$, and each element $(x_1, \dots, x_{d-1}, x_{d+1}, \dots, x_k)$ of $G_1\times\dots\times G_{d-1}\times G_{d+1}\times \dots\times G_k$, the map that sends each $y_d$ such that $(x_1, \dots,$ $x_{d-1},$ $y_d,$ $x_{d+1}, \dots,$ $x_k) \in A$ to $\phi(x_1, \dots,$ $x_{d-1},$ $y_d,$ $x_{d+1}, \dots,$ $x_k)$ is a Freiman homomorphism (of order 2). In this paper, we prove that for each such map, there is a multiaffine map $\Phi \colon G_1 \times\dots\times G_k \to H$ such that $\phi = \Phi$ on a set of density $\Big(\exp^{(O_k(1))}(O_{k,p}(\delta^{-1}))\Big)^{-1}$, where $\exp^{(t)}$ denotes the $t$-fold exponential. Applications of this theorem include: $\bullet$ a quantitative inverse theorem for approximate polynomials mapping $G$ to $H$, for finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector spaces $G$ and $H$, in the high-characteristic case, $\bullet$ a quantitative inverse theorem for uniformity norms over finite fields in the high-characteristic case, and $\bullet$ a quantitative structure theorem for dense subsets of $G_1 \times\dots\times G_k$ that are subspaces in the principal directions (without additional characteristic assumptions).
item.dc:creator: W. T. Gowers, L. Mili\'cevi\'c

item.title: Minor summation formula of hyperpfaffians and Selberg integrals
item.description: arXiv:2008.09776v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the previous paper (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 120, 2013, 1263--1284) H. Tagawa and the two authors proposed an algebraic method to compute certain Pfaffians whose form resemble to Hankel determinants associated with moment sequences of the classical orthogonal polynomials. At the end of the paper they offered several conjectures. In this work we employ a completely different method to evaluate this type of Pfaffians. The idea is to apply certain de Bruijn type formula and convert the evaluation of the Pfaffians to the certain Selberg type integrals. This approach works not only for Pfaffians but also for hyperpfaffians. Hence it enables us to establish much more generalized identities than those conjectured in the previous paper. We also investigate some Pfaffians related to classical $q$-orthogonal polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Masao Ishikawa, Jiang Zeng

item.title: Affine and cyclic affine equivalence of rotation-symmetric S-boxes
item.description: arXiv:2203.00778v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A rotation-symmetric S-box on $n$ bits is a vectorial Boolean function that commutes with the right cyclic shift and is therefore determined by a single Boolean function. The map $\chi$ used in Keccak is a well-known example. Ordinary affine equivalence allows arbitrary invertible affine transformations, which need not preserve rotation symmetry. We introduce \emph{cyclic affine equivalence}, in which the implementing transformations each have an invertible $k$-circulant linear part with $\gcd(k,n)=1$ and a translation vector fixed by the shift. For $n\ge3$, the two relations give the same classes of rotation-symmetric permutations exactly when $n$ is an odd prime for which $2$ is a primitive root. In every other dimension $n\ge3$, explicit constructions exhibit affine classes containing several cyclic affine classes. We derive exact class-size formulas, count cyclic affine classes for $3\le n\le9$, and classify a four-bit family of $\chi$-siblings under both relations. Finally, we characterize when a permutation is affinely equivalent to a rotation-symmetric one and apply the criterion to the Ascon S-box.
item.dc:creator: Tron Omland, Pantelimon Stanica

item.title: Veronese sections and interlacing matrices of polynomials and formal power series
item.description: arXiv:2404.12989v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The concept of a fully interlacing matrix of formal power series with real coefficients is introduced. This concept extends and strengthens that of an interlacing sequence of real-rooted polynomials with nonnegative coefficients, in the special case of row and column matrices. The fully interlacing property is shown to be preserved under matrix products, flips across the reverse diagonal and Veronese sections of the power series involved. These results and their corollaries generalize, unify and simplify several results which have previously appeared in the literature. An application to the theory of uniform triangulations of simplicial complexes is included.
item.dc:creator: Christos A. Athanasiadis, David G. Wagner

item.title: New classes of reversible cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2411.00721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cellular automata find applications in cryptography, error correction, theoretical computer science, and the simulation of physical and biological processes. We say that a Boolean function is a proper lifting if its induced cellular automaton is reversible. This paper introduces new classes of proper liftings, constructed through compositions of landscape functions, and explores their cryptographic potential by computing indicators relevant to differential and linear cryptanalysis. We combine theoretical and computational methods to obtain a complete classification of proper liftings for diameters up to $6$. Several open problems and conjectures are posed along the way.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Tron Omland

item.title: Satisfying sequences for rainbow partite matchings
item.description: arXiv:2502.03105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal F_1,\ldots, \mathcal F_s\subset [n]^k$ be a collection of $s$ families. In this paper, we address the following question: for which sequences $f_1,\ldots, f_s$ do the conditions $|\mathcal F_i|>f_i$ imply that the families contain a rainbow matching, that is, there are pairwise disjoint $F_1\in \mathcal F_1,\ldots, F_s\in \mathcal F_s$? We call such sequences {\em satisfying}. Kiselev and the first author showed that $f_1 = \ldots = f_s=(s-1)n^{k-1}$ is satisfying for $s>470$, verifying the conjecture by Aharoni and Howard. This is the best possible if we insist that the families are of the same size. However, it turns out that much more can be said about asymmetric restrictions. In this paper, we investigate this question in several regimes and in particular answer the questions asked by Kiselev and Kupavskii. We use a variety of methods, including concentration and anticoncentration results, spread approximations, and the Combinatorial Nullstellenzatz.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Kupavskii, Elizaveta Popova

item.title: Edge-vertex degree based Zagreb index and graph operations
item.description: arXiv:2505.05999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph $G$ consists of two parts, the vertices and edges. The vertices constitute the vertex set $V(G)$ and the edges, the edge set. An edge \( e=xy \), \( ev \)-dominates not only the vertices incident to it but also those adjacent to either \( x \) or \( y \). The edge-vertex degree of $e,$ $deg^{ev}_{G}(e),$ is the number of vertices in the $ev$-dominating set of $e$. In this article, we compute expressions for the $ev$-degree version of the Zagreb index of several unary and binary graph operations.
item.dc:creator: Amitariddhi Sinha, Somnath Paul

item.title: Arbitrary orientations of Hamilton cycles in directed graphs of large minimum degree
item.description: arXiv:2505.09793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1960, Ghouila-Houri proved that every strongly connected directed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $n$ contains a directed Hamilton cycle. We asymptotically generalize this result by proving the following: every directed graph $G$ on $n$ vertices and with minimum degree at least $(1+o(1))n$ contains every orientation of a Hamilton cycle, except for the directed Hamilton cycle in the case when $G$ is not strongly connected. In fact, this minimum degree condition forces every orientation of a cycle in $G$ of every possible length, other than perhaps the directed cycles.
item.dc:creator: Louis DeBiasio, Andrew Treglown

item.title: Planar induced paths via a decomposition into non-crossing ordered graphs
item.description: arXiv:2509.17835v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In any graph, the maximum size of an induced path is bounded by the maximum size of a path. However, in the general case, one cannot find a converse bound, even up to an arbitrary function, as evidenced by the case of cliques. Galvin, Rival and Sands proved in 1982 that, when restricted to weakly sparse graphs, such a converse property actually holds. In this paper, we consider the maximal function $f$ such that any planar graph (and in general, any graph of bounded genus) containing a path on $n$ vertices contains an induced path of size $f(n)$, and prove that $f(n) \in \Theta (\log n/\log \log n)$ by providing a lower bound matching the upper bound obtained by Esperet, Lemoine and Maffray, up to a constant factor. We obtain these tight bounds by analyzing graphs ordered along a Hamiltonian path that admit an edge partition into a bounded number of sets without crossing edges. In particular, we prove that the guaranteed size of an induced path when the ordered graph can be partitioned into $2k$, resp. $2k+1$, sets of non-crossing edges, is $\Theta_k((\log n/\log \log n)^{1/k})$, resp. $\Theta_k((\log n)^{1/(k + 1)})$.
item.dc:creator: Julien Duron, Hugo Jacob

item.title: A Generalisation of Sperner's Theorem Using Weighted Chains
item.description: arXiv:2509.26493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We find the (unique) largest subset of $\{0, 1, 2\}^n$ such that it contains no two elements, one of which is coordinatewise greater than the other, but strictly greater on at most $k$ coordinates. To do so, we decompose the cube into weighted chains. In Appendix B we present a new proof of Sperner's theorem we found while working on this problem.
item.dc:creator: Ya\"el Dillies, Matthew Johnson, Aleksandra Kowalska

item.title: Monadic Second-Order Logic of Permutations
item.description: arXiv:2511.02386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Permutations can be viewed as pairs of linear orders, or more formally as models over a signature consisting of two binary relation symbols. This approach was adopted by Albert, Bouvel and F\'eray, who studied the expressibility of first-order logic in this setting. We focus our attention on monadic second-order logic. Our results go in two directions. First, we investigate the expressive power of monadic second-order logic. We exhibit natural properties of permutations that can be expressed in monadic second-order logic but not in first-order logic. Additionally, we show that the property of having a fixed point is inexpressible even in monadic second-order logic. Secondly, we focus on the complexity of monadic second-order model checking. We show that there is an algorithm deciding if a permutation $\pi$ satisfies a given monadic second-order sentence $\varphi$ in time $f(|\varphi|, \operatorname{tw}(\pi)) \cdot n$ for some computable function $f$ where $n = |\pi|$ and $\operatorname{tw}(\pi)$ is the tree-width of $\pi$. On the other hand, we prove that the problem remains hard even when we restrict the permutation $\pi$ to a fixed hereditary class $\mathcal{C}$ with mild assumptions on $\mathcal{C}$.
item.dc:creator: V\'it Jel\'inek, Michal Opler

item.title: Chip-firing on the Lattice of Nonnegative Integer Points
item.description: arXiv:2601.09125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chip-firing on a directed graph is a game in which chips, a discrete commodity, are placed on the vertices of the graph and are transferred between vertices. In this paper, we study a chip-firing game on the lattice of nonnegative integer points on the $x$-$y$ plane, where we start with $2^n$ chips at the origin. When we fire a vertex $v$, we send one chip to each out-neighbor. We fire until we reach a stable configuration, a distribution of chips where no vertex can fire. We study the intermediate firing configuration: a table that assigns to each vertex the total number of chips that reach it. We prove that the nonzero entries of the stable configuration correspond to the odd entries of the intermediate firing configuration. The intermediate firing configuration consists of three parts: the top triangle, the midsection, and the bottom triangle. We describe properties of each part. We study properties of each row and the number of rows of the intermediate firing configuration. We also explore properties of the difference tables, which are tables of first differences of each row of the intermediate firing configuration.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Inagaki, Tanya Khovanova, Austin Luo

item.title: An assortment of problems in permutation patterns: unimodality, equivalence, derangements, and sorting
item.description: arXiv:2602.16355v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We collect open problems in permutation patterns on four themes: rank-unimodality in the permutation pattern poset and log-convexity of principal classes, Wilf-equivalence and shape-Wilf-equivalence, the enumeration of derangements in permutation classes, and sorting by stacks in series, generalized stacks, and restricted containers (C-machines).
item.dc:creator: Vincent Vatter

item.title: On problems of Erd\H{o}s and Baumann-Briggs on minimising the density of $s$-cliques in graphs with forbidden subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2602.17412v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using flag algebras, we prove that the minimum density of $8$-cliques in a large graph without an independent set of size $3$ is $491411/268435456+o(1)$, thus resolving a new case of an old problem of Erd\H{o}s [Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutat\'o Int. K\"ozl. 7 (1962) 459-464]. Also, we establish some other results of this type; for example, we show that the minimum $s$-clique density in a large graph with no independent set of size 3 nor an induced 5-cycle is $2^{1-s}+o(1)$ when $s=4,5,6$. For each of these results, we also describe the structure of all extremal and almost extremal graphs of large order $n$. These results are applied to give an asymptotic solution to a number of cases of the problem of Baumann and Briggs [Electron. J. Combin. 32 (2025) P1.22] which asks for the minimum number of $s$-cliques in an $n$-vertex graph in which every $k$-set spans a $t$-clique.
item.dc:creator: Levente Bodn\'ar, Oleg Pikhurko

item.title: On a stable partnership problem with integer choice functions
item.description: arXiv:2603.24433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a far generalization of the well-known stable roommates and non-bipartite stable allocation problems. In its setting, one is given a finite non-bipartite graph $G=(V,E)$ with nonnegative integer edge capacities $b(e)\in{\mathbb Z}_+$, $e\in E$, in which for each vertex (``agent'') $v\in V$, the preferences on the set $E_v$ of its incident edges are given via a choice function $C_v$ acting on the vectors in ${\mathbb Z}_+^{E_v}$ bounded by the capacities and obeying the standard axioms of substitutability and size monotonicity. We refer to the related stability problem as the stable partnership problem with integer choice functions, or SPPIC for short. Extending well-known results for particular cases, we give a solvability criterion for SPPIC and develop an algorithm of finding a stable solution, called a stable partnership, or establishing that there is none. Moreover, in general the algorithm constructs a pair $(x,{\cal K})$ such that $x\in {\mathbb Z}_+^E$ and ${\cal K}$ is a set of pairwise edge-disjoint odd cycles in $G$ satisfying the following properties: if ${\cal K}=\emptyset$, then $x$ is a stable partnership, whereas if ${\cal K}$ is nonempty, then a stable partnership does not exist, and in this case, the set ${\cal K}$ is determined canonically. Our constructions essentially use earlier author's results on the corresponding bipartite counterpart of SPPIC. Keywords: stable marriage problem, stable roommates problem, stable partition, stable allocation, choice function
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Discrete Applied Math., Vol.397, 2026, pp.345-359. Free share link until Dec.15, 2026: https://authors.elsevier.com/a/1n-qk_,OC1pQzC
item.dc:creator: Alexander V. Karzanov

item.title: Tropical Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2606.24339v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of tropical regularity as a generalization of tropical smoothness and present a geometric classification conjecture for tropical regular cycles. Roughly, the conjecture predicts that every regular tuple either forms a regular fibration or descends via a lattice projection to one of finitely many minimal-model cycles. Our main results establish this conjecture in three fundamental cases:unmixed regular tuples $(T,\ldots,T,[F])$ with $L(T)=\{0\}$ and $[F]$ spanning its ambient space; regular tropicalizations of complete intersections with generic coefficients; and regular tropical $2$-cycles satisfying the Hodge index inequality and spanning their ambient space.
item.dc:creator: Linxuan Li

item.title: Combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of fence posets
item.description: arXiv:2607.11225v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a fence poset P , we define a new statistic on permutations, denoted by blP, that provides a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the order polynomial of P , answering a question of Ferroni, Morales, and Panova (2025). Using the fact that the base polytope of a lattice path matroid can be decomposed into order polytopes of fence posets, we also obtain a combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients of the Ehrhart polynomial of the base polytope of Schubert matroids, answering a question of Stanley (1999). As an application of this statistic, we establish the first nontrivial lower bound for the linear coefficient of the Ehrhart polynomial of an order polytope. Finally, we conjecture generalizations of this statistic to skew-shape posets and circular fence posets.
item.dc:creator: Yakob Kahane

item.title: Generalised flip order on the faces of nestohedra
item.description: arXiv:2607.20132v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tamari lattices and weak Bruhat order are classical posets on the vertices of associahedra and permutohedra. These posets are particular instances of the \emph{flip order} on the vertices of graph associahedra. We present here a generalisation of the flip order to all the faces of nestohedra, encoded in terms of hypergraphs. For right-filled hypergraphs, we characterise our order in terms of generalised inversions. As an application, we describe shuffle products on faces of suitable nestohedra as sums over intervals in this order.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Louis Curien, B\'er\'enice Delcroix-Oger, Jovana Obradovi\'c

item.title: Weight-constrained universal sequences
item.description: arXiv:2607.22350v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2011/12, Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams showed that a binary universal sequence can be constructed containing all $n$-tuples of Hamming weight either $r$ or $r+1$ for every possible $r$, and no others. In this paper we examine extensions of this result that require choosing a weight-like function applying to $n$-tuples with symbols taken from an alphabet of arbitrary (finite) size. We consider three possible such weight functions, and in each case establish an analogous result to that of Ruskey, Sawada, Stevens and Williams.
item.dc:creator: Chris J Mitchell, Peter R Wild

item.title: Removable matchings in $2$-connected graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.06918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A matching $M$ of a $2$-connected graph $G$ is \emph{removable} if $G-M$ is $2$-connected. We prove that, for every integer $d\ge4$, every $2$-connected graph with at least $2d$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$ has a removable matching of size $d$. This improves the previously known lower bound $d-2$ for $d\ge5$ to the optimal value $d$, answering a question of Li, Zhou, Fujita, and Mao. We also show that a $2$-connected graph on at least six vertices with minimum degree at least $3$ has a removable matching of size $3$ if and only if it is not a wheel. Our proofs use edge contraction and the structure of \emph{minimal non-removable matchings}.
item.dc:creator: Jinik Hwang, Ringi Kim

item.title: Multicolor Ramsey numbers of ordered matchings
item.description: arXiv:2609.08157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an ordered graph $H$ and an integer $q\geq2$, let $r_{<}(H;q)$ denote the $q$-color ordered Ramsey number of $H$. Conlon, Fox, Lee and Sudakov asked whether, for every $q\geq3$, there is a constant $c_q$ such that $r_{<}(M;q)\leq n^{c_q\log n}$ for every ordered matching $M$ on $n$ vertices. We answer this negatively in a strong form: for every $q\geq2$, there is $c_q>0$ such that almost every perfect matching $M$ on $[n]$ satisfies $$r_{<}(M;q)>2^{c_q(\log n)^q/(\log\log n)^{q-1}}.$$ This matches the general upper bound up to a factor of $(\log\log n)^{q-1}$ in the exponent. We also give two applications. First, we prove a lower bound conjectured by Fox, He and Wigderson for multicolor Ramsey numbers of acyclic digraphs. Second, we strengthen a result of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt by giving a superquasipolynomial lower bound on the maximum chromatic number of $M$-free ordered graphs, for almost every perfect matching $M$ on $[n]$.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Li

item.title: The Distance Between the Adjacency Spectral Center and the Characteristic Set of a Tree
item.description: arXiv:2609.16943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $S(T)$ denote the adjacency spectral center of a tree $T$, and let $C(T)$ be its characteristic set. We determine the maximum possible distance $\Delta_n:=\max_{|V(T)|=n}\operatorname{dist}_T(S(T),C(T))$ for every $n\ge 3$. It turns out that $\Delta_n=0$ for $3\le n\le 11$, that $\Delta_{12}=1$, and that $\Delta_n=\left\lfloor\frac{n-11}{2}\right\rfloor (n\ge 13)$. More generally, if the two sets are at distance $d\ge 2$, then the branch issuing from a closest vertex of $S(T)$ in the direction of $C(T)$ contains at least $2d+5$ vertices, while the complementary part of the tree contains at least $6$. We also establish structural restrictions in the equality case and completely classify the extremal trees of every odd order $n\ge 17$: there are exactly four nonisomorphic extremal trees, consisting of two brooms and two double brooms. Our proofs exploit the opposite extremal behaviour of paths for the adjacency spectral radius and for the bottleneck Perron value.
item.dc:creator: Chaochao Zhu, Shipei Hu, Jingfu Huang, Qin Yue

item.title: The Face Lattice of any Simplicial Polytope is Hamiltonian
item.description: arXiv:2609.19938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the cover graph of the face lattice of every simplicial polytope admits a Hamilton cycle. Moreover, any two distinct facets can be prescribed as the neighbors of the full polytope on this cycle. By duality, the face lattice of every simple polytope is Hamiltonian as well. This proves the simplicial and simple cases of a conjecture of Behrooznia, Brenner, Merino, M\"utze, Rieck, and Verciani (SODA26). The proof uses a line shelling in both directions. The forward shelling partitions the faces into Boolean intervals, whose cover graphs are cubes. The reverse shelling gives a second partition, on which we construct a perfect matching by adding or removing a fixed vertex in each interval. This matching connects the cubes of the first partition. A theorem of Gregor then completes it to a Hamilton cycle using only edges within these cubes. The same argument applies to shellable simplicial spheres, although without the prescribed neighbors of the full complex in this case. Using Chari's shelling construction of perfect matchings, we also obtain Hamiltonicity for polytopes with at most one facet that is not a simplex.
item.dc:creator: Robert Lauff

item.title: Four collinear points or six visible points
item.description: arXiv:2609.21035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every finite planar set of at least $880$ points contains four collinear points or six pairwise visible points.
item.dc:creator: Stijn Cambie

item.title: Disproving Conjectures on the Davenport and Narkiewicz Constants
item.description: arXiv:2609.29878v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Davenport constant $\DD(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is a classical invariant arising from the arithmetic of ideal class groups of number fields. Closely related to the Davenport constant is the first Narkiewicz constant $\Nark_1(G)$, which arises in the quantitative study of algebraic integers and their factorizations. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured in 2006 that $\DD(G)\leq \sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ while Narkiewicz and \'Sliwa conjectured in 1982 that $\Nark_1(G)=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ where $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ are the invariant factors of $G$. Both are central conjectures concerning arithmetic invariants arising from the theory of number fields. In this paper, we disprove both conjectures. Moreover, we show that, for every fixed $r\geq5$, both $\DD(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ and $\Nark_1(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ are unbounded over finite abelian groups of rank $r$. We develop a probabilistic representation technique to establish a uniform upper bound for the Davenport constant: $$ \DD(G)\leq\frac{16}{5}\,\rr(G)\exp(G). $$ Our bound gives the first improvement of the classical van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk estimate: $\DD(G)\leq\exp(G) \left(1+\log\frac{|G|}{\exp(G)}\right) \leq\exp(G)\bigl(1+(\rr(G)-1)\log\exp(G)\bigr)$, by removing the logarithmic dependence on the exponent from this classical estimate, replacing it with the absolute constant $16/5$. Their bound stood unimproved since its establishment in 1969. The existence of $C=16/5$ also brings us closer to the most challenging conjecture on the Davenport constant, namely the Emde Boas--Kruyswijk Conjecture in 1969, which predicts that $\DD(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1.$ As a further application of our results, we disprove a conjecture of Girard in 2008 concerning cross numbers, an invariant with deep roots in the arithmetic of number fields and Krull monoids.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang

item.title: A quasipolynomial inverse theorem for the $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ norm in the high characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2609.33733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an inverse theorem for the Gowers uniformity norm $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ with quasipolynomial bounds in the case when $p \geq k$. The inverse theorem follows from a quasipolynomial structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms, which are a natural generalization of Freiman homomorphisms to maps of several variables. The proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is the central result of the paper and rests on three main ingredients: algebraic regularity method, abstract Balog-Szemer\'edi-Gowers theorem and the theory of multilinear maps defined on multilinear varieties. The last ingredient originates from an earlier work of Gowers and the author, and is significantly expanded in this paper. In particular, once the theory of such maps is in place, the proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is relatively short, especially compared to the previous quantitative results in the inverse theory of Gowers norms.
item.dc:creator: Luka Mili\'cevi\'c

item.title: Matching algebras and their Dunkl subalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.34260v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite simple graph $G = (V, E)$, we consider the quotient algebra $\mathcal M(G)$ of the polynomial ring in the variables $u_e$ (for $e \in E$) by the ideal generated by all products $u_e u_f$ for non-disjoint edges $e$ and $f$ (including all squares $u_e^2$). This quotient is called the matching algebra of $G$, since it has a basis indexed by the matchings of $G$. In this quotient, we define a subalgebra $\mathcal D(G)$ generated by the signed incidence sums $\theta_v=\sum_{e=(v,w)}u_e-\sum_{e=(w,v)}u_e$ for all $v \in V$ (where all edges of $G$ are oriented arbitrarily); we call this the Dunkl matching algebra. We show that, as a graded vector space, $\mathcal D(G)$ is dual to the span of all polynomials $p_M = \prod_{(i,j) \in M} (x_i - x_j)$, where $M$ ranges over all matchings of $G$. For the complete graph $K_n$, the latter span is a direct sum of two-row Specht modules (one in each degree); thus its Hilbert series is that of the Catalan triangle, and, in characteristic zero, the Dunkl matching algebra can be presented by linear and quadratic relations. For arbitrary graphs, we formulate the saturation problem of deciding when the selected matching Specht generators $p_M$ in a given degree $k$ span the full two-row Specht module $S^{(n-k,k)}$. We show that saturation in degree $k$ forces $k$-connectivity, that saturation in degree $2$ is equivalent to $2$-connectivity, and that $k$-linked graphs are saturated in degree $k$. We also prove saturation in every possible degree whenever the complement of $G$ is a matching. We show that the Dunkl matching algebra equals the full matching algebra exactly for forests, and give an explicit Hilbert series formula for unicyclic graphs.
item.dc:creator: Darij Grinberg, Anatol Kirillov, Boris Shapiro

item.title: Real-rootedness and ultra log-concavity of rank-two matroid Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.37439v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial of a rank-two matroid with exactly three parallel classes is real-rooted whenever its smallest parallel class has size at most three. This bound is sharp: the loopless rank-two matroids with parallel-class sizes $(4,561,600)$ and $(4,a,a+29)$, for all sufficiently large integers $a$, have $h^*$-polynomials that are not real-rooted. By matroid duality, these examples disprove Ferroni's real-rootedness conjecture even for cycle matroids of theta graphs. Nevertheless, every matroid of rank two or corank two has a positive $h^*$-coefficient sequence that is ultra log-concave of order equal to the polynomial's degree. In particular, the unimodality conjecture holds in both cases.
item.dc:creator: Houshan Fu

item.title: On the asymptotics of the Erd\H{o}s-Rogers function
item.description: arXiv:2609.37987v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Erd\H{o}s-Rogers function $f_{\ell,s}(n)$ is the largest order of a $K_\ell$-free induced subgraph guaranteed to exist in every $K_s$-free graph on $n$ vertices. While this function is well understood for $s=\ell+1$, the case where $s$ is much larger than $\ell$ has remained wide open. A long-standing lower bound of Sudakov states that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\geq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$, while a recent result of Brada\v{c} shows that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell-1}{s-1}+o(1)}$. In this paper, we close this gap asymptotically by proving that $f_{\ell,s}(n)= n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$. More precisely, we prove that for all $2\leq \ell<s$, we have $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s-\ell}+o(1)}$. Our proof builds on Brada\v{c}'s recent tight construction for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers, which can be viewed as the $\ell=2$ case of our result.
item.dc:creator: Domagoj Brada\v{c}, Oliver Janzer, Rik Sarkar

item.title: Upper bounds on the Tur\'{a}n density of projective hypergraphs over a finite field
item.description: arXiv:2610.01084v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a prime power $q\geq2$ and an integer $m\geq2$, let $PG(m,q)$ denote the $m-$dimensional projective hypergraph over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. Employing the $\mathsf{L}^p-$method and using the incidence structure, we establish the Tur\'{a}n density of $PG(m,q)$ \begin{equation*} \pi(PG(m,q))\leq\begin{cases} \left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{q}} & \text{ if } m=2, \left(1-\frac{1}{(q+1)|E(PG(m-1,q))|}\right)^{\frac{1}{1+q^{m-1}}} & \text{ if } m\geq3. \end{cases} \end{equation*} The previously known upper bound on its Tur\'{a}n density was $1-\binom{q^m}{q}^{-1}$. As a consequence of our estimate, this upper bound is improved for each prime power $q\geq3$ and for each dimension index $m\geq2$. For a positive integer $t$, let $B_{t}[PG(2,q)]$ be the $(q+1)-$graph formed by taking $t$ copies of the $PG(2,q)$ that shares a common edge. Using the $\mathsf{L}^p-$method, we establish that the upper bound of the Tur\'{a}n density of $B_{t}[PG(2,q)]$ is $\left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)^{\frac{1}{qt}}$.
item.dc:creator: Subhankar Dash, Kaushik Majumder

item.title: Making Every Number from 1 to N Under a Fixed Cycle of $+$, $\times$, $-$, $\div$
item.description: arXiv:2610.10095v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Start with the number $2$. At each move, combine two numbers already made, but the operations must be used in the fixed repeating order $+,\times,-,\div$. We ask for the fewest moves needed to make every integer from $1$ to $N$. Since $2$ is already one of the numbers we want and each move makes at most one new number, at least $N-1$ moves are needed. We show that $N-1$ moves are also enough for every $N\ge 9$. Conventional induction cannot work, because a division that comes right after a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ produces numbers already made. Instead we extend a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ to $\{1,\dots,3P\}$ all at once, which counting shows is the smallest multiplicative extension $P\to kP$ that can work, and then adjust the last few moves to reach every other $N$. For $9\le N\le 33$ we give explicit sequences, found by computer search.
item.dc:creator: Sean Lesmana, Theodore Tjugiarto

item.title: Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.10559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We systematically explore the relationship between edge-connectivity and Lin--Lu--Yau curvature for graphs. The intuition is that a connected graph with large Lin--Lu--Yau curvature should also have large edge-connectivity, and vice versa under suitable conditions. We prove that the edge-connectivity of a connected graph is bounded lower by the product of its minimum degree, its Lin--Lu--Yau curvature and the constant $\frac{3}{2}$. We also provide two lower bounds on the edge-connectivity of a graph that guarantee positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature, and discuss the sharpness of these bounds.
item.dc:creator: Ziming Zhou, Shenggui Zhang

item.title: A rank bound for bases and circuits in binary matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.11829v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(b(M)\), \(d(M)\), and \(r(M)\) denote the number of bases, the number of circuits, and the rank of a matroid \(M\), respectively. Using a weighted count of fundamental circuits, we prove that every nonempty simple binary matroid \(M\) with no coloops satisfies \[ 2b(M)\ge(r(M)+1)d(M), \] with equality if and only if \(M\) is isomorphic to the Fano matroid. This settles a conjecture recorded by Oxley in 1983. For every \(e\in E(M)\), we also establish the deletion bound \(b(M\backslash e)\ge d(M)\) and characterize its equality cases. The deletion bound yields a sharp linear lower bound for basis growth under successive series extensions. Finally, under a circuit-size exclusion condition, every pair \((C,e)\) with \(C\) a circuit of a prescribed size and \(e\in C\) can be assigned a distinct basis containing \(C-e\).
item.dc:creator: Houshan Fu

item.title: Disproving two conjectures on the cospectrality of complete tripartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.18636v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The spectral distance between two non-isomorphic graphs of the same order is the lp-distance between their ordered adjacency spectra, and the cospectrality of a graph G on a family Gn is the minimum such distance from G to another graph in Gn. Abdollahi and Zakeri (Ars Math. Contemp. 22(1) (2022) P1.06) conjectured that, for every n >= 4 and for p in {1, 2}, the cospectrality of the complete tripartite graph Kn,n,n among all graphs on 3n vertices is attained exactly at Kn-1,n,n+1. We disprove both conjectures for every n >= 4. As a counterexample we use the graph Hn = (n - 1)K1 nabla (K1 union Kn,n), whose spectrum we determine. It yields cs(1)(Kn,n,n) <= 1 + o(1) and cs(2)(Kn,n,n) <= 1/2 + o(1) as n -> infinity, contrary to the conjectured values. We also study the cospectrality of Kn,n,n for p = 2, asymptotically, among complete multipartite graphs with possibly added isolated vertices. We conclude the paper by posing a conjecture that Hn is the unique graph nearest to Kn,n,n for p in {1, 2} and every n >= 3, and a problem asking whether every connected graph H with sigma(2)(Kn,n,n,H) < 2/3 has an adjacency matrix of rank at most 5.
item.dc:creator: Irena M. Jovanovi\'c, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

item.title: Graph and Hypergraph Counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation Conjecture Beyond $n^{k-1}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18876v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a fixed $k$-graph $F$, let $h_F(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex $k$-graph with $\text{ex}(n,F)+q$ edges. Let $c(n,F)$ be the minimum number created by adding one edge to an extremal $F$-free $k$-graph. We construct stable counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for every $k\ge2$. The ratio $h_F(n,q)/(q c(n,F))$ tends to zero over ranges extending beyond $n^{k-1}$. For graphs, we give examples of every chromatic number at least three. In particular, there is a graph $F$ for which this ratio tends to zero for $1\le q=o(n^{4/3})$. For $k\ge3$, we use connected linear expansions of $G=(M_a\cup K_{1,b}\cup I_h)\vee K_{m_1,\ldots,m_{k-1}}$. Under explicit parameter conditions, the ratio tends to zero for $1\le q=o(n^{k-1+(b-1)/(a+b-1)})$ when $b\ge k+1$. We prove the exact Tur\'an theorems for both constructions and determine their unique extremal graphs and hypergraphs. Keywords: supersaturation; extremal graph; linear hypergraph; graph expansion; stability.
item.dc:creator: Liping Zhang, Qinghai Liu, Qinfei Tang, Yanmei Hong

item.title: An improved upper bound on the chromatic number of the n-dimensional sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.32408v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this short note, we obtain upper bounds on the chromatic numbers of spheres using recent improvements in bounds for Euclidean space. We show that $\chi (S^n_{R}) \leq (\xi_R + o(1))^n$, where $\xi_R = \frac{3\sqrt 3}{2}(1-\frac{1}{4R^2}) $ and $\chi(S^n_R)$ denotes the chromatic number of the $n$-dimensional sphere of a fixed radius $R$.
item.dc:creator: A. I. Bikeev, V. A. Voronov, A. M. Raigorodskii

item.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.37173v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, K\"uhn and Osthus from 2016. The proof combines a local pairing argument based on the lopsided Lov\'asz local lemma with cycle decompositions of random graphs.
item.dc:creator: Jifu Lin, Heng Yang

item.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
item.description: arXiv:2610.39021v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.
item.dc:creator: Keith McNulty

item.title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39228v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of L\'aszl\'o Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.
item.dc:creator: G. Militaru

item.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.40032v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: B\'erczi, Geh\'er, Imolay, Lov\'asz, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,\alpha}$, $0<\alpha<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue

item.title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
item.description: arXiv:2610.41555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Haiman conjectured that for every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{\lambda,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings. Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_\mu$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Keith McNulty

item.title: Categorification of $k$-Schur functions and refined Macdonald positivity
item.description: arXiv:2505.23202v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a substantial part of the categorification framework for $k$-Schur functions proposed in Chen's Ph.D.\ thesis, written under the supervision of Mark Haiman. More precisely, we realize $k$-Schur functions as the graded characters of a distinguished family of objects in a certain module category and establish module-theoretic analogues of several foundational properties of $k$-Schur functions. A final part of Chen's framework predicts a homological characterization of modules admitting filtrations by these distinguished objects; we establish this characterization under an additional combinatorial hypothesis. In addition, we unconditionally prove that modules arising in this framework admit filtrations whose subquotients are affine Demazure modules of level $k$. As a consequence, modified Macdonald polynomials expand positively in the characters of affine Demazure modules. This may be viewed as a homological refinement of Macdonald positivity, arising from an intrinsic $\mathrm{ext}$-orthogonality condition on the corresponding Garsia--Haiman modules. We also prove the combinatorial hypothesis for $m \le 2k$ in the appendix and verify it computationally for $m\leq 19$, yielding $k$-Schur positivity of modified Macdonald polynomials in these cases. Our approach builds on our previous work on the algebraic and geometric realization of Catalan symmetric functions, a class encompassing both $k$-Schur and Hall--Littlewood functions.
item.dc:creator: Syu Kato

item.title: Dispersion models on a circle: universal properties and asymptotic results
item.description: arXiv:2507.00737v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consider a sequence of masses $m_0,m_1,...$ arriving uniformly at random at some points $u_0,u_1,...$ on the unit circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ (or on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, in the discrete version). Upon arrival, each mass undergoes a relaxation phase during which it is dispersed, possibly also at random. This process can model many physical phenomena, such as the diffusion of liquid in a porous medium. In the discrete case, it can model parking (related to additive coalescence and hashing with linear probing) in which the cars are permitted to follow random displacement policies. The dispersion policies considered in the paper ensure that at time $k$, after the successive dispersions of $m_0,\cdots,m_{k-1}$, the total covered region has Lebesgue measure $m_0+\cdots+m_{k-1}$. Furthermore, during the dispersion of a given mass, the covered domain increases continuously, except when it merges with another covered connected component (CC). We show a very general exchangeability property for the sequence of covered CC. Additionally, we demonstrate a universal spacing property between these CC, and a notable general result: if the $(u_i)$ are independent and rotationally invariant, then the number of free (not covered) CC follows a binomial distribution whose parameters depend solely on the number and total mass of arrived particles. Furthermore, conditional on the number of CC, the sizes of the free CC follow a simple Dirichlet distribution in the continuous case, regardless of the dispersion policy considered and the values of the masses. We also characterize the distribution of the occupied space. In the second part of the paper, we study the total cost associated with these models for various cost models, and establish connections with the additive coalescent. We also provide an asymptotic representation of the limiting covered space as the number of masses goes to infinity.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Marckert, Zo\'e Varin

item.title: Catalan Semirings
item.description: arXiv:2510.05045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Catalan semirings, which are additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups belong to a natural family of transformation monoids known as Catalan monoids. There are two kinds of Catalan semirings, whose properties differ substantially. We address the Finite Basis Problem for individual Catalan semirings of each kind and their representations by Boolean triangular matrices. Furthermore, we characterize the varieties and pseudovarieties generated by all Catalan semirings of each kind.
item.dc:creator: Sergey V. Gusev, Mikhail V. Volkov

item.title: $k$-path graphs: experiments and conjectures about algebraic connectivity and $\alpha$-index
item.description: arXiv:2511.21524v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This work presents conjectures about eigenvalues of matrices associated with $k$-path graphs, the algebraic connectivity, defined as the second smallest eigenvalue of the Laplacian matrix, and the $\alpha$-index, as the largest eigenvalue of the $A_{\alpha}$-matrix. For this purpose, a process based on [Discrete Applied Mathematics 164 (2014) 297-303] is presented to generate lists of $k$-path graphs containing all non-isomorphic 2-paths, 3-paths, and 4-paths of order $n$, for $6 \leq n \leq 26, 8 \leq n \leq 19$, and $10 \leq n \leq 18$, respectively. Using these lists, exhaustive searches for extremal graphs of fixed order for the mentioned eigenvalues were performed. Based on the empirical results, conjectures are suggested about the structure of extremal $k$-path graphs for these eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Rafael L. de Paula, Claudia M. Justel, Carla S. Oliveira, Milena S. Carauba

item.title: Structural and Spectral Properties of Strictly Interval Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2512.01175v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we deal with a subclass of chordal graphs, which are simultaneously strictly chordal and interval, the strictly interval graphs. We present a new characterization of the class that leads to a simple linear recognition algorithm. Next we introduce a new subclass of strictly interval graphs, the $SI$-core graphs, that are non-split and non-cograph graphs and show that several elements of the new class are Laplacian integral
item.dc:creator: Claudia Justel, Lilian Markenzon

item.title: On uniform large genus asymptotics of Witten's intersection numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.15233v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Following ideas from [14], we give a uniform large genus asymptotics for primitive psi-class intersection numbers on the moduli space of stable algebraic curves, and extend this result including insertions of zeros in a certain uniform way. Application to a particular formal solution of the Painlev\'e I equation is given. We also use a method from [14] to give a new proof of the polynomiality conjecture on large genus asymptotic expansions of psi-class intersection numbers.
item.dc:creator: Jindong Guo, Di Yang, Don Zagier

item.title: Identification to Subclasses of Chordal Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2604.24325v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An identification of two vertices \(u\) and \(v\) in a graph replaces them with a new vertex that is made adjacent to every vertex of \(N(u)\cup N(v)\setminus \{u,v\}\). We study the \(\mathcal{H}\)-Identification problem, which is to decide whether a given graph \(G\) can be transformed (``identified'') to a graph in \(\mathcal{H}\) by applying at most \(k\) vertex identifications. We determine the classical and parameterized complexity of this problem for various subclasses \(\mathcal{H}\) of chordal graphs, obtaining an almost complete picture for two parameters: \(k\) and \(n-k\). We also consider the Identification problem, which is to test, for two given graphs \(G\) and \(H\), whether \(G\) can be identified to \(H\). We determine the parameterized complexity of this problem when \(H\) is a graph from one of our testbed classes, taking the number of simplicial vertices of \(H\) as the parameter.
item.dc:creator: Petr A. Golovach, Laure Morelle, Dani\"el Paulusma

item.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2606.11987v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lifted product codes are an important family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, as they were the first QLDPC code family shown to be asymptotically good. Understanding the structure of their parity-check matrices $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$, as well as the associated Tanner graphs, is essential for analyzing their decoding behavior and error-floor performance. In this work, we show that the Tanner graphs of $H_{\mathsf{X}}$ and $H_{\mathsf{Z}}$ are indeed isomorphic, and investigate their graph-theoretical structure. We establish conditions ensuring the connectivity of these graphs and provide bounds on their minimal absorbing sets, providing new insight into the combinatorial structures influencing decoding performance.
item.dc:creator: Ragnar Freij-Hollanti, Kirsten D. Morris, Patricija \v{S}apokait\.e

item.title: The five vertex model on a rectangle
item.description: arXiv:2606.22004v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive a determinantal expression for the inhomogeneous asymmetric five vertex model in a rectangular geometry with arbitrary boundary conditions at the bottom and top. Standard non-intersecting lattice path, or free fermion, approaches are not applicable and the determinantal form thus is not immediate.
item.dc:creator: Jan de Gier, Richard Kenyon, Michael Wheeler, Yuyang Zhou

item.title: Discrepancy for Random Linear Codes
item.description: arXiv:2606.24471v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that random linear codes (RLCs) possess nearly optimal discrepancy-type properties in a broad range of settings. Our main results are two general discrepancy theorems: one controls all translates of a fixed test, and the other controls large families of Fourier-pseudorandom tests. Two motivating examples follow: First, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for list-decoding from errors above capacity. More precisely, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1 - \frac{1}{n}\log_q|B_\rho| + \varepsilon$, where $|B_\rho|$ is the volume of a radius-$\rho$ Hamming ball in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, satisfies $|C \cap B| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot |B|}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all radius-$\rho$ Hamming balls $B$ with high probability. This significantly strengthens the best prior results, which follow from work by Blinovsky (1987, 1990) and Levitin (1988) on the covering properties of RLCs. Second, over prime fields, RLCs behave essentially like unstructured random codes for zero-error list-recovery, and list-recovery from erasures, above capacity. More precisely, for a prime $q>2$ and input list size $2\leq \ell\leq q-1$, an RLC $C\subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of rate $1-\log_q \ell+\varepsilon$ will satisfy $|C \cap S| = (1\pm o(1)) \frac{|C|\cdot \ell^n}{q^n}$ simultaneously for all combinatorial rectangles $S=S_1\times S_2\times\cdots\times S_n$, where $|S_i|=\ell$ for all $i$, with high probability. An analogous result also holds when we can bound $|S_i|$ only for some of the $i$'s. We use this to show the abundance of locally leakage-resilient $n$-party linear ramp secret sharing schemes with any linear reconstruction threshold and sublinear threshold gap $O(n/\log n)$ over fields of polynomial size $q=\Theta(n^\gamma)$ for a constant $\gamma\in(0,1/5)$. Prior work was stuck at reconstruction thresholds above $n/2$ for both threshold and ramp schemes.
item.dc:creator: Dean Doron, Tal Leonov, Jonathan Mosheiff, Henrique Navas, Nicolas Resch, Jo\~ao Ribeiro

item.title: Avalanche homology of digraphs via sandpile dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.26786v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce avalanche homology as a new (di)graph homology theory, based on the dynamics of the sandpile model. Avalanche homology is the simplicial homology of the avalanche complex generated from the sets of unstable vertices at the time steps of the sandpile dynamics. In this work we focus on digraphs, and our main results give the homotopy types of the avalanche complex for directed paths and directed cycles for certain initial configurations of the sandpile dynamics. Even for such simple digraphs a wide range of topologies can arise, and we compare this to the directed flag complex and to the recently introduced burning homology. Furthermore, the dynamics yields very naturally a filtered simplicial complex, and hence persistent avalanche homology.
item.dc:creator: Henri Riihim\"aki, Jason P. Smith

item.title: A classification of nearly Gorenstein monomial ideals
item.description: arXiv:2608.15955v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We classify nearly Gorenstein monomial ideals over an arbitrary field. In dimension zero, we compute the canonical trace ideal using a graph on the socle monomials. In positive dimension, we prove a dimension bound under unmixedness and a connectedness condition, with weaker assumptions on the canonical trace ideal.
item.dc:creator: Sora Miyashita

item.title: A Two-regime Khintchine Inequality and an Improved Bound on the Degree-1 Fourier Weight for Linear Threshold Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.27908v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Khintchine inequality provides a lower bound on the expected absolute value of a weighted sum of independent Rademacher random variables.
