In the classical setting, when the coefficient vector has unit Euclidean norm, this lower bound is a constant, with equality attained only by a simple family of extremal configurations. A refinement due to De, Diakonikolas, and Servedio, referred to as the \emph{linear Khintchine inequality} in this work, strengthens this estimate by establishing a lower bound that depends linearly on the distance of the coefficient vector from the extremal set. In this paper, we present a refined analysis of this dependence on the weight vector. Our results reveal a phase transition in the rate of improvement: when the dimension exceeds six, the lower bound undergoes an abrupt change as the weight vector deviates from the minimizer. Additionally, we improve the slope constant in linear Khintchine inequality. As a consequence, we establish an improved lower bound on the degree-1 Fourier weight for linear threshold functions $\mathbf W^{\leq1}[f]\geq0.55100929$, marking progress towards a conjecture of Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Fang, Tianyu Wang

item.title: Surjectivity of the Enots Wolley Sequence
item.description: arXiv:2609.18054v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the Enots-Wolley sequence, a greedy sequence defined by local divisibility and coprimality conditions, contains every positive integer with at least two distinct prime divisors. This resolves an open conjecture by Shannon and Sloane. The only analytic number-theoretic inputs are the prime number theorem and Mertens' estimate for reciprocal primes.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Myles Nichols

item.title: The lattice covering density of the regular octahedron
item.description: arXiv:2609.23210v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the lattice covering density of the regular octahedron is $9/8$, establishing the optimality of the classical body-centered cubic covering. A hypothetical lattice covering of smaller density would yield a lattice basis whose six Kuhn tetrahedra each fit in a translate of the octahedron. A sharp determinant bound then gives a contradiction. As a consequence, the maximum order of an undirected Abelian Cayley graph with three generators and their inverses and diameter at most $k$ is $\frac{32}{27}k^3+O(k^2)$ as $k\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Yanlu Lian, Fei Xue

item.title: A Quaternary Legendre Pair of Length 64
item.description: arXiv:2609.25573v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A quaternary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ is a pair of sequences over $\{\pm 1, \pm \mathrm{i}\}$ whose periodic autocorrelations sum to $-2$ at every nonzero shift. We give a quaternary Legendre pair of length $64$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported construction at this length.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Verma

item.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
item.description: arXiv:2609.28059v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$ of infinite words over finite alphabets. For recurrent aperiodic words using exactly $\ell\geq 2$ letters, we prove the sharp lower bound $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq k+\ell-1$ and give a structural characterization of those words attaining equality for every $k\geq 1$. Without assuming recurrence, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every positive integer $k$. For aperiodic words over $\ell\geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq(\ell-1)(k-\ell+2)$, for all positive integers $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell-1)k}+O_{\ell}(1)$. We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, for every positive integer $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset\mathbb{N}_0$ whose bipartite incidence graph is a forest. This graph has two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_0$ as its vertex classes, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng

item.title: A New Upper Bound for 7-Universal Tournaments
item.description: arXiv:2610.06891v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A tournament is $k$-universal if it contains every tournament on $k$ vertices as a subtournament. We give a 7-universal tournament on 14 vertices, improving the upper bound of 15 due to Zhang and Szeider. Together with their lower bound, it follows that the smallest 7-universal tournament has 13 or 14 vertices.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Verma

item.title: Subspace Uncertainty and Sharp Sampling Thresholds on the Boolean Cube
item.description: arXiv:2610.12358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a known finite-dimensional model subspace, classical Gaussian regression theory guarantees that least squares eventually attains the parametric rate, with prediction error scaling as the subspace dimension divided by the sample size. Yet subspaces with the same number of unknown coefficients can require very different sample sizes to reach this regime. For subspaces of polynomials on the Boolean cube, a fundamental question is how restrictions on degree and ambient dimension jointly determine this threshold. Our main result sharply characterizes the worst-subspace minimax sample threshold over a substantial parameter range, revealing an exponential dependence on degree and precisely quantifying the joint effects of degree, ambient dimension, and subspace dimension. A small modification of our lower-bound construction reveals a strong separation: a single subspace can admit noiseless recovery with optimal sample complexity independent of degree, yet require essentially the worst-case sample size, exponential in degree, to attain the noisy parametric rate. To establish the sampling lower bound, we sharpen the Polyanskiy-Samorodnitsky uncertainty principle (J. Funct. Anal., '19) to uniformly optimal precision and extend its concentration guarantee to large subspaces in which every function concentrates most of its energy on one shared Hamming ball. The sampling upper bound follows from the sharp moment bound of Kirshner and Samorodnitsky (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, '21) combined with empirical-process bounds.

item.title: NP-hardness of additive approximation for generalized Tur\'{a}n problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.16358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a graph $T$ and a nonempty family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ denote the maximum number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{F}$-free subgraph of a host graph $G$. Alon and Shikhelman [Algorithmica, 2022] conjectured that if $e(T)> 0$ and no member of $\mathcal{F}$ is a subgraph of a blow-up of $T$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$, approximating $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ within an additive error of $n^{v(T)-\varepsilon}$ is NP-hard for an input graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. Previous advances toward this conjecture include the resolution of the canonical case $T=K_2$ by Alon, Shapira, and Sudakov [Ann. of Math., 2009], as well as the case of $\operatorname{ex}(G,K_m,K_k)$ by Alon and Shikhelman. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for every bipartite graph $T$ and every clique $T$. Our proof reductions combine several techniques, including iterative leaf additions, symmetric rooted extensions, and random transversals. Together, they encode the optimal value of the NP-hard Max $r$-Colorable Subgraph problem into the objectives $\operatorname{ex}(G, T, \mathcal{F})$ for a suitably constructed graph $G$.

item.title: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2610.18905v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Qudit codes often inherit the parameters of qubit codes, but not necessarily their correctable erasures. We show that a code encoding one qudit of dimension D into seven such qudits that corrects every erasure Steane's code corrects exists exactly when D is a power of 2; for the qutrit color code, exactly when D is odd. This needs no stabilizer assumption: these codes are, up to local unitaries, stabilizer codes of qubits, respectively prime-power qudits. The two patterns differ in one line, which completes the Fano plane only where 1+1=0. As ideal secret sharing schemes, these codes exist exactly where classical ones do: entanglement does not help, unlike for Euler's 36 officers. The same arithmetic makes the entropy cones of qubit and odd-dimensional stabilizer states incomparable from six parties on. At five, the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, answering an open question.

item.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.23684v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

item.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27551v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.

item.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30845v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.

item.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Structural Reductions, Transverse Products, and Fixed-Codimension Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.37421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, product constructions, and fixed-codimension stability. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument yield an explicit bound \[ \mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}. \] For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two configuration splits off a common linear factor, so $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities. We further prove that for every fixed codimension $c$, the sequence $\mathcal{N}(k,k+c)$ is eventually constant. In codimension three, a sharper normal-span argument gives \[ \mathcal{N}(k,k+3)=\mathcal{N}(7,10)\qquad(k\geqslant7), \] where the numerical threshold uses the computer-assisted theorem $\mathcal{N}(1,3)=7$. The structural and stability results are otherwise independent of that numerical input.

item.title: Abelianization and moment maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.42123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$. We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.
